FILE: DM Notes\Story\Prologue\Session -1 - Beyond Journey's End.md
========================================

---
lastSync: Wed Nov 06 2024 22:24:11 GMT+0000 (Greenwich Mean Time)
tags:
  - Session
  - Solaum
  - Story
  - Stormshroud-Legion
  - Solaris-Vanguard
  - Villentiari-Isle
  - Third-Convergence
  - Circle-of-Elements
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---
# Premise
Players bring their former characters from Tegan's campaign and then get transported to the past after the battle. They land on the last day of [[Solari Calendar|Shumi]] (The last month of the year) 693 [[Dating|IOG]]. Everything is unrecognisable to them. The 20th [[Military of Solara|Rikati]] of [[Solara]] shows up and demands they show their identification as they don't have any they are forced to fight, revealing that they are [[Elementals]], which leads to their capture.

This then leads to them being brought to [[Solaum]] and executed on the spot (all except [[Aelius]] as he has ties to Solara). In the crowd watching their execution is their new player characters (not yet created).
# Scenes
- The Present
	- The former lands of the [[Stormshroud Legion]] (modern day Villentiari Isle)
		- The site of the final battle between the elements and their proxies
		- The Camp of the [[Solaris Vanguard]]
			- The [[Great Tent]] (their sleeping quarters)
- The Past
	- [[Villentiari Isle]]
		- The forest which will become the site of the final battle in the future.
		- Camp of the 20th [[Military of Solara|Rikati]] of [[Solara]].
	- Solaum
		- Execution Preparation area
		- Outside the [[Dolumi Solaunao]], near the [[Obelisk of Origin]].
# Story
The party celebrates the end of the struggle they had been facing for countless days, adventuring across the lands of the [[Stormshroud Legion]]. As they begin to celebrate, [[Decimus]], one of the members of the [[Solaris Vanguard]] (the secret society emulating the practices of the old nation of [[Solara]]), tells them stories of the forgotten nation, in which [[Aelius]] happily divulges. They then retreat to their chambers to sleep.

They awake to see the camp deserted. This desertion is not typical of The Solaris Vanguard, as it is not a part of the virtue of hospitality honoured by the nation of Solara, thusly Aelius is shocked. On the floor is a circle of the [[Elements]], a symbol distrusted by the [[Setting/Cultures/Solari|Solari]] as recounted by Aelius.

The party proceeds to stand in their places, [[Thandoril Sunfire|Thandoril]] follows suit. Once this happens the circle begins to emanate a strange light and the sun begins to be eclipsed by the moon. A beam of light envelops the elementals and the a minor [[The Fourth Convergence|Convergence]] takes place, sending the party back in time to just before the [[Second Convergence]].

The party awakes from unconsciousness. Dazed and confused, the party is left to wonder as to what just happened, thusly, they begin looking for answers; the circle beneath their feet has disappeared and appears to have been swallowed with grass and dirt. Their surroundings have suffered the same fate. A land that was once a camp of the Solaris Vanguard seems to have become dense forest. Upon further observation, it seems the [[Great Tent]] has also vanished following the preceding events. After a great search, they can see smoke rise above the canopy in the distance to the North. The party now has their heading.

Heading this way brings them to a relatively modern looking path in the forest. The wood has clearly been artificially cleared to make way for the cobblestone road. A road this maintained must be kept in this state by a powerful entity. They continue to follow the road towards the smoke to look for answers. This road is the best road they had walked on for a long time as it is made for heavy use.

As they continue their walk, they see a marching [[Military of Solara|rikati]] coming into view with great fires and a massive supply chain in tow. The amount of soldiers numbers in the thousands. Upon seeing the adventurers the scouts of the rikati report back to the [[Centurion]]. The centurion sends an envoy ahead to greet the travellers and asks for documentation of their residence within Solara.

The envoys speaks in a [[Solari (Language)|language the party cannot understand]], except for complex vocabulary. All except Aelius who can understand the language to a basic degree. Despite this he cannot respond, he can only understand the words spoken at him. They attempt to explain that they do not have any documentation in [[Common (Language)|Common]]. This effort was not founded though and the envoy just wanders back to the rikati and informs the Centurion of the transgression and their strange language. The rikati continues its march along the path, encountering the party, attacking them unawares and capturing them for being [[Elementals]].

The rikati continues its march following the capture of their new powerful prisoners, having handcuffed them using [[Elemental Suppression Cuffs|elemental suppression cuffs]] to prevent them from using their powers. Eventually the party arrives at the [[Camp of the 20th Rikati of Solara]], near [[Ducata]]. Here the Centurion questions the party of their intentions, but cannot get a word out of them. Not liking the lack of co-operation from the party, the rikati boxes them up to be shipped to the capital of Solara, [[Solaum]].

During their travels, the party can hear lots of conversations; the sound of a horse's gallop; the onloading of their containers onto a ship; the sounds of the sea for hours; the offloading of their containers and then the sounds of a bustling city. Throughout their journey they cannot see any of the events taking place.

Suddenly, the crates open up to reveal a detention centre and another soldier of a rikati. He is carrying chains that he ties around the wrists and ankles of the prisoners, including the party. He then leads the prisoners out to the execution grounds in front of the [[Dolumi Solaunao]] and the [[Obelisk of Origin]].

The great crowd around the prisoners watch in anticipation as the executioner slowly moves up the line with his axe, beheading each and every one of the prisoners. The excitement draws to a peak as the executioner announces to the crowd that the following prisoners have all been captured for being illegal, dangerous elementals. To which the crowd cheer in excitement to their impending death. The executioner swings his axe and beheads each one-by-one until the last party member is dead.

The screen turns black.
# Story Beats
- Party Celebrating the defeat of the [[Stormshroud Legion]].
- Party is taken to the Camp of the [[Solaris Vanguard]].
- Party is taken into the [[Great Tent]] by [[Decimus]] who tells them a story about [[Solara]].
- The party wakes up to find the camp deserted.
- The party finds the [[Circle of the Elements]] in the middle of the camp where the bonfire was and cause the [[Fourth Convergence]], causing them to get sent back in time to just before the [[Second Convergence]]
- The party awaken to find a forest around them
- The party find smoke in the distance and follow it to a road
- The party is discovered by the 20th [[Military of Solara|Rikati]] of Solara
	- Upon being contacted by the [[Setting/Cultures/Solari|Solari]], [[Aelius]] realises he can understand them a little bit.
- The party enters combat against the 20th Rikati of Solara, reveal they are elementals, and lose.
- The party is captured and taken back to the [[Camp of the 20th Rikati of Solara]]
	- The party is questioned but cannot understand [[Solari (Language)|Solari]]
- The party is shipped to [[Solaum]]
- The party is executed
# Characters
- The Party
	- [[Kraven Redblade]]
	- [[Lyre Hallowstream]]
	- [[Aelius]]
	- [[Alea]]
	- [[Bronlyl Battleale]]
	- [[Derf Drayniw]]
	- [[Thandoril Sunfire]]
- [[Solaris Vanguard|The Solaris Vangaurd]]
	- [[Decimus]]
- [[Solara]]
	- The 20th [[Military of Solara|Rikati]] of Solara
		- The Envoy
		- The Centurion
		- ~4800 Soldiers
	- [[Solaum]]
		- The executioner
		- Various guards

>## Philosophical Works
> |  |   |
> | ---- | --- |
> | __Main Interests__ | Magic, Politics, Ethics, Metaphysics, Natural Science, Botany, Elemental Magic |
> | __Notable works__ | [[Atiric Texts]], numerous lost grimoires |
> | __Notable Ideas__ | What makes a human, dictatorship |

__Atiri__ (350 - 434 [[Dating|IOG]]) was a scholar, mage, and philosopher of [[Solara|the Solari Replublic]] and the founder of the [[Atiri Centre of Magical Excellence]] as well as the author of many texts and grimoires including the [[Atiric Texts]]. He taught by [[Varma]] an [[Setting/Cultures/Aeia|Aeian]] Elf.

Atiri is known to have lived a troubled life. He was born in [[Solaum]], capital of the Solari Republic. His father and mother both died when his house was raided at the age of 7. He was then captured and sold into slavery at [[Itrea]], one of the holiest cities in the world and gateway to [[Mount Aemi]]. There he was taught by Varma the ways of magic and magical studies. This experience moulded his world-view and his outlook on studying. He remained in the tutelage of Varma until he disappeared at age 62. He then travelled back to Solaum to found his academy.

Among his contemporaries and those who knew him he was seen as a man of moderation, but also of great power. Many would freeze upon gazing upon him due to the sheer amount of mana he possessed. His writing was considered abstruse and meandering by his teacher and his students. He was also considered to have a greater understanding of magic than everyone other than Varma, though Varma preferred to be moderate with his utilisation of the craft.

Due to his contributions and legendary life many works are attributed to his name though most are fakes.

# Life
## Early Life
Atiri was born on [[Dating|9th of Minumi 350]] to poor parents in the slums of Solaum outside the [[Buno Walls]]. His parents were not remarkable in any way and he described them in his writings as "dull and uninteresting." His parents were however descendants of the founders of Solaum and thus he was ethnically [[Setting/Cultures/Solari|Solari]]. His birthname is unknown as he had forgotten it shortly after his kidnapping and was referred to as only "horabos" which means slave in [[Aeikas]]. As a result of his upbringing he was fluent in both [[Setting/Languages/Solari|Solari]] and Aeikas. He was given his name by Varma. As far as we know he had no siblings and was an only child, however, we do know all his family died during the kidnapping.

During his childhood Solara was undergoing rapid expansion, conquering neighbouring tribes in [[Setting/Regions/Asheri|Asheri]]. This rapid expansion brought new challenges for Solara including placating the recently conquered peoples and assimilating them into a hostile society. Atiri's father was involved in the war to some unknown degree. Atiri had no formal education growing up in his familial home, however Atiri enjoyed writing, especially journaling and poetry, which he had learned from his mother. He dropped writing poems when he met his teacher, Varma.

Sometime in [[357 - Atiri Gets Captured|357 IOG Atiri's familial home was razed, his family was killed and he was captured]] by some [[Setting/Cultures/Margos|Margos]] peoples. During his capture he was a slave to the travellers who went around pillaging Solari settlements and are known to have travelled east with their captives, looking to make a profit selling their spoils. It is during this time he was sold at the city of [[Setting/Settlements/Cities/Itrea|Itrea]].

In Itrea, Atiri was treated as second class but he had time to be mindful of himself and be true to his religion. Itrea is a holy city and, as the [[Setting/Religions/Solari|Solari Religion]] is highly syncretic, he found time to worship his gods in the various temples scattered around the city. His slave masters called him "[[Setting/Languages/Aeikas|horabos]]" as a derogatory term meaning "slave," due to this treatment he forgot his birthname. He was frequently beat as a form of disciplining which was illegal in Itrea, but he could not speak up because he was not a citizen of the land.

Around the age of 15 when getting beat he discovered he was a [[Setting/Elements/Fire|Fire elemental]] and accidentally burnt down his masters' house. He also caused a small fire in the surrounding area, in the process he killed his masters. To avoid death he escaped Itrea and ran in to the woods where he lived until he found Varma.

## Magical Career
Atiri found himself practicing magic in the forest outside of [[Setting/Settlements/Cities/Itrea|Itrea]] just under [[Mount Aemi]] for two years. Lighting and starting simple fires. When he was found by [[Varma]] he was on the verge of accidentally causing a forest fire because the fire he had lit had starting burning out of control. According to Atiri's own account he was seen as Varma than little more than a nuisance when he first found him and was blamed for putting the forest out of balance and potentially angering the forest's spirit. Atiri found this laughable because he had never heard of the landed - or nature's - spirits before.

### Varmic Teachings
Varma would end up adopting Atiri as his primary apprentice in 367 IOG. During this time Atiri would end up being bestowed his name by his master: "Aetor" in his master's tongue, which means "The One Who Knows" and is transliterated into Solari as _Atiri_.

Varma would teach Atiri everything he deemed him worthy of knowing bit by bit, including magic that has long since been forgotten. This includes nature and draconic magic as well as magic from other elements by transferring his power into him. 

According to Atiri's accounts he Varma would wake him at dawn every day and make him practice magic until the sun set at the end of the day, only stopping to alleviate themselves and eat. Varma would often disappear and hunt for food however, sometimes as though they were nomads rather than settled, civilised beings. He also recounted that it seemed as though Varma already had hundreds, if not thousands of years of untapped knowledge. He also though as though Varma knew something Atiri didn't at all times, also that Varma seemed to have experience in training others other than himself.

#### Ascent of Mount Aemi
Atiri often claimed that Varma would express that being in tune with nature around you during a fight gave you the favour of the spirits of nature and that they would help you out. To be this in tune required that you understood and appreciate the earth for the simplest things.

One day Varma woke Atiri up at an untimely hour before sunrise and told him to follow him up Mount Aemi. On the way up, he said that Varma was recounting how every leaf, every tree and every blade of grass had its own soul, as did the breeze, the moon and each star in the sky and so did the mountain. Atiri was taking in his every word as if he was going to say something different or teach him something revolutionary.

Upon reaching the peak, Varma sat himself on the floor and stared straight towards the direction of the easterly wind, claiming both of them will be able to meet [[Aushuzi]], Goddess of the Dawn, on a day like this. They both watched the sun rise together and while Varma claimed he could feel her presence, Atiri said nothing happened and he couldn't feel anything. Varma said he would not be able to feel anything until he was truly in tune with nature.

Atiri continued to ascend the mountain every morning, before dawn, when the wind blew east. He claimed to have never met Aushuzi before he died.

#### The Disappearance of Varma
On 15th Narimi 412 IOG (The day of the moon of war in the Solari calendar), which corresponds to 1-1-4212 in the [[Aeia Foundation Calendar]] also known as the [[Dark Night Festival]], Atiri woke up and noticed that something was different about where he had been, the world felt empty and there was a notable absence where something once filled the air surrounding the nature in the area. He claimed the plants looked in despair but he couldn't describe how he knew. He noted the wind was also blowing South to North that day and he didn't climb the mountain as something was eerie.

He waited patiently for Varma to come to greet him every day for the past 45 years of his life, but he never showed. He says there was not a trace left behind of his leave and not a footprint in the mud, just an emptiness in the air as if he was never there before and never there after.

It was after this he decided to take what he knew and head back to Solaum.

### Travels
Before heading back to Solaum he realised he needed to earn some money. He then started to perform miracles and barter for food, using hunting, gathering and foraging skills he had learned from Varma to get him between settlements. He tended to not want to stay too long in any one place but had numerous followers by the time he had reached the next road on his path.

He started spreading his learnings and wisdom during this period and spread knowledge in what he called the "Varmic Teachings." He would say to people to meet him in Solaum and said they would know when he arrived, without saying how. This is when he finally understood what it meant to be in touch with nature.

Through his lessons he managed to garner a small fortune, but one large enough that he could construct his academy in Solaum.

## Return to Solaum

# Premise

The players are all gathered in the capital city of [[Amphos]], in the Amphosian Despotate. On a relatively normal day, a delivery is due to reach the temple containing elemental stones and an important book to go alongside them. This is when certain individuals attempt to either guide others to the right path or intercept the waiting stones to take them for profits.

After the heist the party is driven from Amphos by the city guards. They are now due north to find a place to rest.

# Scenes

- [[Amphos]]
	- [[Northern Slums]]
		- Market Street
		- Plaza
			- Public House
		- [[Riley]]'s [[Riley's House|House]]
	- [[Temple to Tolaume]]
		- Outside the temple
		- The Main chamber
		- The Temple Vault (inner chamber)
		- The Temple Pronaos

- [[Amphos-Aklebe Road]]

		- Room 107

# Story

Set approximately 1000 years after the end of campaign 1 (on 1st Hanomi 1782 [[Dating|IOG]]), the world is now a very different place, following the migrations from the north, the [[Solara|Solaran Empire]] has fallen and fractured in to the [[Amphosian Despotate]] (de-jure and de-facto Solaran Empire, or Eastern Solaran Empire) and various other successor states including the [[New Solaran Republic]] which now controls only the [[Vincum Peninsula]] part of the region of [[Asheri]]. Despite this the influence of the Solaran Empire has lead to the spread of Solari culture, language and law leading to immense societal innovation throughout the world and has made the [[Solari (Language)|Solari language]] (once the common language of the empire) a prestige language in many places. In places where it is not, which is mainly the eastern portion of the old empire now ruled by the Amphosian Despotate, the prestige language of the old Solari Empire, [[Aeikas]], the prestige language and common language in these areas.

Because of the breakdown of many trade routes, climate changes, disease and the destruction of the institutions that the Solaran Empire once had in place, many places, cities, towns and villages have seen extreme de-population; even affecting places outside of the once great empire as logistical networks faltered. Great cities such as [[Solaum]] which once bolstered a population of 1,000,000 people now only host around 30,000 people. The largest city on the planet, and richest, is [[Amphos]] and hosts a population of around 200,000, still in the process of depopulation at this point however.

# Story Beats

- [[Riley]] was observing the [[Northern Slums]] Market Street from rooftop
- Riley pounced down beside [[Ellowen]] and stole an apple
- Riley leapt over [[Big Beefy Bob]] and stole [[Big Beefy Bob's Little Orange Hat]]
- Riley entered the plaza and ran into [[Yvaquis]] and her [[Yvaquis's Former Travelling Party|band of travellers]]
- Riley goes home and hears from [[Campaign 2 - DM Notes/Notable NPCs/Wrensu]] about the [[Elemental Stones]] being transported to the [[Temple to Tolaume]].
	- Ellowen overhears this.
- Yvaquis hears about the stones ability to perfectly grind herbs from her travelling party.
- Wrensu informs Riley that they will need muscle to break into the temple and Riley says he ran into a strong person earlier today.
- At midnight, Riley performs his heist on the temple and is followed closely by Ellowen, Big Beefy Bob takes out the temple guard and Yvaquis walks in through the front door to enter the inner chamber.
	- Riley finds the top entrance to the vault and is drawn to the [[Fire Stone]]
	- Ellowen finds the door to the vault and is drawn to the [[Water Stone]]
	- Yvaquis follows Ellowen and is drawn to the [[Earth Stone]]
	- Big Beefy Bob follows Ellowen and picks up a black stone and breaks it
	- Ellowen grabs the [[Atiric Texts|book]].
- Yvaquis discovers Riley is a cat.
- Yvaquis's rock talks to her through her mind
	- Yvaquis thinks she is insane
- Riley is called the "Feline Cat Hero" by the locals
- Big Beefy Bob finds [[Frank the Rock|Frank]] on the ground.
- Riley goes home to find Wrensu missing and the place ransacked. There he finds a note on the ground with the writing "Academy" on it.
- Big Beefy Bob and Yvaquis go to [[Magic Academy of Amphos|the academy]] with Ellowen where guards outside the [[Keep of the Aurelian Vale Family in Amphos]] call her the "Dragon Slayer."
- Big Beefy Bob, Yvaquis and Ellowen are at the academy. In the Office of the [[Head of the Arcane]], Ellowen is alone with the Head of the Arcane wherein she is informed of the [[Elemental Stones]] and the [[Twelve Trials of the Elementals]]. 
- Riley breaks into the Protected Archive of the Soul Stone through a window that doesn't actually exist.
- Big Beefy Bob is drawn to the [[Soul Stone]] on the other side of the door to the Protected Archive of the Soul Stone. He starts banging on the door.
- Riley is driven to near-insanity and activates the Soul Stone's protection mechanism making it launch to its chosen protector.
- Big Beefy Bob comes into the possession of the Soul Stone.

- Riley sees Wrensu midst interrogation.
- Riley retreats and the stones compel their possessors to follow.
- Riley watches his house be torched to the ground with his lute inside.
- The party head North-West.

- Guards from the Aurelian Vale Keep catch up to them and call for Ellowen, who is a part of the house of Aurelian Vale, Ellowen's stone protected her by disguising her.
- Riley hides in a nearby tavern in the slums that contains rum and becomes alcohol-dependant. He also finds a [[Missing Person's Poster for Evangeline Marquis|poster of a missing princess from Eivia]].
- Riley becomes brave because of intoxication and pelts the guards with bottles of rum, causing them to become staggered, allowing the party to escape.
- They continue North-West and end up at the [[The Heavy Head Inn]], along the road to [[Aklebe]].
- They buy a room to stay at the inn.

---
title: Session 2 - The Tavern
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

# Premise

The party take on a small job clearing a tavern storage room of rats in exchange for a promised letter. What appears to be a simple task quickly escalates into excessive violence, improvised magic, and collateral damage to the tavern’s produce.

While completing the job, the party uncovers a letter detailing pirate activity near [[Aklebe]] and the existence of a [[The Zoraneset|well-armed trading war galley]] heading toward [[Mount Aemi]]. This information establishes their next destination and hints at greater dangers beyond the tavern.

Further exploration of the inn reveals locked guest rooms, signs of religious secrecy, stolen personal belongings, and the presence of a mysterious traveller. Through conversation and careful observation, one party member realizes this individual is far more important than he appears — a royal traveling incognito on a diplomatic mission.

The session transitions the party from survival-level adventuring into political and maritime intrigue.

# Scenes

- Tavern Interior
    - Storage Room (Rat infestation)
    - Guest Rooms (Locked and unlocked)
    - Bathing Room
    - Common Room / Bar
- Upstairs Guest Quarters
- Tavern Exterior

# Story

[[Dating|2nd Hanomi 1782 IOG]], 06:00 - 12:30

The party awake at the tavern seeking a letter and are told they must first clear rats from the establishment’s storage room. After unlocking the door, they discover the infestation consists of several giant rats hiding among food crates.

Combat quickly becomes chaotic. One rat is brutally dismembered, splattering blood across apples and crates. Another is magically desiccated into dust through necrotic magic. The final rat survives long enough to injure [[Big Beefy Bob]] before being chilled, stabbed, and finished off by [[Riley]], who is eager to finally perform thier role in combat.

With the rats dealt with, the party rummage through the storage room and discover a letter discussing pirate attacks on ships near [[Aklebe]]. The letter also grants passage aboard [[The Zoraneset|a heavily armed trading war galley]] heading toward [[Itrea]], establishing [[Aklebe]] as the party’s next destination.

Exploring the upstairs rooms, the party break into several guest chambers. One room belongs to a wealthy and educated occupant, containing maps, writing implements, and an illegal religious idol. The idol is identified but left behind to avoid future consequences. A hidden lute is discovered and taken, creating an unspoken debt between party members.

During this time, Riley takes his first bath in a very long while, emerging significantly cleaner, though only marginally more respectable.

Back in the common room, the party interact with a [[Tukue Potes|quiet, well-dressed traveller posing as a poor man]]. Through shared food, awkward conversation, and careful investigation, [[Ellowen]] recognizes the man as the Prince of [[Amphos]] traveling in disguise. He is on a diplomatic mission to the holy city-state of [[Itrea]]. Ellowen keeps this revelation secret, suspecting both danger and opportunity if the truth were revealed.

The session ends with the party having secured their letter, identified their next destination, and unknowingly becoming entangled in royal diplomacy.

# Story Beats

- Party accept a rat-clearing job to obtain a letter.
- Storage room door is opened.
- Giant rats are fought and killed in various dramatic ways.
- Big Beefy Bob is injured during combat.
- Pirate-related letter is discovered.
- Aklebe is established as the next destination.
- Party break into upstairs guest rooms.
- Illegal religious idol is identified but not stolen.
- A lute is discovered and taken.
- Riley takes a bath for the first time in a long time.
- Party befriend a mysterious traveller.
- Ellowen identifies the traveller as the Prince of Amphos.
- Diplomatic tensions are quietly introduced.

# Characters

- The Party

    - [[Big Beefy Bob]]
    - [[Ellowen]]

- Tavern Staff
    - Innkeeper
- [[Royal Court of Amphos]]
    - [[Tukue Potes]] (Prince of Amphos) (incognito)
    - [[Tabtab]] (as "The Apothecary")
- Pirates of Aklebe (mentioned)

---
title: Session 3 - The Path
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

# Premise

The party continue their journey north toward [[Aklebe]], traveling through quiet countryside marked by ancient graves, forgotten stonework, and signs that the land itself holds deep elemental significance.

What begins as uneventful travel turns meaningful when the party discover a broken tombstone and a nearby stone circle tied to an [[Hasharshagetes|ancient traveler]] and [[Bon|long-lost peoples]]. These discoveries hint that the world’s elemental forces were once understood — and interacted with — very differently.

The journey takes a violent turn when the party are ambushed by wolves in the forest, forcing them into a desperate fight while already worn down from travel. In the aftermath of the battle, the party encounter an ancient golden tree growing from magically charged ground. Though the tree itself is not magical, interaction with it reveals powerful truths about elemental forces, the land, and the party’s growing connection to both.

The session ends with the party reaching [[Aklebe]], battered, altered, and carrying knowledge they do not yet understand.

# Scenes

- Road toward [[Aklebe]] 
    - Meadows and burrows
    - [[Broken tombstone]]
	- [[Ancient Stone Circle]]
	- Forest Path
		- Forest Clearing (Wolf ambush)
		- Forest Path (Aftermath and travel)
			- Forest Clearing (Golden Tree)
		- Road toward Aklebe
- [[Aklebe]]
    - Harbour
    - [[Murotes's House|Lodgings]]

# Story

[[Dating|2nd Hanomi 1782 IOG]], 13:00 - 20:30

The party travel north along the road toward [[Aklebe]], passing through open meadows filled with burrows, flowers, and scattered trees. The land is quiet but clearly well-used. Along the roadside, they discover a broken tombstone partially buried in overgrowth. Investigation reveals the name _[[Hasharshagetes]]_ carved in an ancient language.

Through discussion and lore, the party recall stories of Hasharshagetes, a legendary traveller and observer from a distant age, associated with early understanding of the world’s elemental forces and the cycle of existence. The tombstone appears less like a grave and more like a marker.

Nearby, the party discover an ancient stone circle attributed to an early people known as the _[[Bon]]_. The stones are covered in mosses of varying colours, each corresponding to known [[Elements|elemental aspects]]. Arcane investigation reveals the area is charged with latent energy, though little can be safely activated. The party note the significance of the site before continuing onward.

As the road narrows and forest thickens, the party begin to notice signs of animal movement. Before they can react, they are ambushed by a pack of wolves emerging from the undergrowth.

Combat is brutal and chaotic. [[Big Beefy Bob]] absorbs repeated attacks and is left badly injured. [[Yvaquis]] destroys one wolf with divine power, while others are brought down through force and magic. The party survive the ambush, but several members are left in critical condition.

In the aftermath, the group stop to tend wounds. Medicine checks clean injuries but do not restore strength. Food and alcohol provide limited comfort. Eventually, magical healing is used to stabilise the party enough to continue.

After several more hours of travel, the party encounter a fork in the path. One route continues forward, while a faint side path leads deeper into the forest. Investigation reveals a strange, ancient golden tree growing in a nearby clearing, and curiosity draws the party toward it.

The golden tree is enormous and impossibly old, estimated to be thousands of years in age. Investigation reveals that the tree itself is not magical; instead, its roots draw power from magically charged stones deep beneath the forest floor. The surrounding land is subtly altered as a result.

Each party member experiences a different reaction when interacting with the tree:

- [[Riley]] finds that alcohol instantly loses its effect and the tree starts burning when he touches it.
- [[Ellowen]] experiences [teleportation via means of turning into water](https://roll20.net/compendium/dnd5e/Misty%20Step#content).
- [[Yvaquis]] experiences overwhelming elemental communion, sensing the planet as an interconnected whole and briefly reshaping the terrain beneath her feet. The earth deforms around her feet.
- [[Big Beefy Bob]] experiences repeated visions through the eyes of a long-dead figure, witnessing mountains, altars, sealed gates, and the containment of catastrophic elemental power and historical understanding tied to long-dead travellers and truths of the land.

Attempts to combine elemental stones with the tree result in unpredictable and dangerous effects, including teleportation, heat, and damage to the tree itself. Casting _Identify_ reveals the tree acts as a conduit and amplifier for elemental power rather than a source. Overuse causes the tree to become unresponsive, and the party eventually decide to stop experimenting.

Returning to the road, the party continue toward [[Aklebe]]. Along the way, they notice enormous footprints filled with water near the roadside and a felled tree blocking further travel north-east but choose not to investigate further.

Upon arrival in [[Aklebe]], the party meet the [[Murotes|Harbour Master]], who offers them [[Murotes's House|lodging]] and proposes a job involving reclaiming [[The Zoraneset|his ship]] through gambling at the [[Panting Shadow]]. Failure would incur a penalty, though this is reduced through negotiation.

That night, the party rest. Most sleep normally, but [[Big Beefy Bob]] experiences disturbing dreams in which whispering voices offer power and [[Atiric Texts|Ellowen's book]] speaks cryptically of memory, loss, and forgotten names. During the night, [[Aushuzi|a magical mishap]] causes [[Big Beefy Bob's Little Orange Hat]] to glow brightly, unnoticed by the others.

The session ends with the party resting in [[Aklebe]], their understanding of the world — and themselves — fundamentally altered.

# Story Beats

- Party travel north toward [[Aklebe]].
- Broken tombstone is discovered and investigated.
- [Hasharshagetes] is identified as a legendary traveller.
- Ancient stone circle of the [[Bon]] is found.
	- Elemental symbolism is observed.
- Party continue into dense forest.
	- Party are ambushed by wolves.
		- Big Beefy Bob is critically injured.
		- Wolves are defeated.
	- Party attempt non-magical and magical healing.
	- Party encounter a fork in the road.
	- Golden tree is discovered.
		- Tree is identified as a conduit, not magical itself.
		- Each party member experiences unique effects.
		- Elemental stones interact unpredictably with the tree.
		- Identify reveals the tree’s true nature.
		- Tree becomes unresponsive after overuse.
	- Party continue toward [[Aklebe]].
	- Giant footprints are noticed and avoided.
- Party arrive at [[Aklebe]]
	- Party meet the Harbour Master.
	- Lodging is secured  
	- Bob experiences prophetic nightmares.

# Characters

- The Party
    - [[Riley]]
    - [[Big Beefy Bob]]
    - [[Ellowen]]
    - [[Yvaquis]]
- Ancient Figures
    - [[Hasharshagetes]] (legendary)
- Creatures
    - Wolves (pack)
- [[Aklebe]]
    - [[Murotes|Harbour Master]]

========================================

---
title: Session 4 - Aklebe, The Panting Shadow, and a Game of Cups
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

# Premise

The party begins their morning at the [[Murotes's House|Harbormaster’s House]] in [[Aklebe]], where tensions from previous sessions linger and the reality of their mission sets in. After investigating their host’s cluttered home and learning of his desperate financial situation due to rampant gambling in the city, the party heads to [[The Panting Shadow|a local gambling den]] to win back a ship.

Inside the den, the party encounters [[Masha]], a mysterious firbolg who joins their cause after a fateful meeting. Amidst high-stakes games of "Poison Roulette" and magical cheating, their pasts begin to catch up with them. [[Ellowen]]’s secret noble identity is nearly exposed by [[Tabtab|a royal apothecary]], and the party successfully secure [[The Zoraneset|a powerful war galley]]. The session concludes with the party boarding their new vessel, preparing to sail toward the mountains with a new ally in tow.

# Scenes

- [[Aklebe]]
    - [[Murotes's House|Harbormaster’s House]]
        - Triangular Bedroom
        - Main Hall (cluttered with maritime gear)
        - Harbormaster's Private Room
    - The Docks
    - [[The Panting Shadow]] (Gambling Den)
- [[The Zoraneset|The War Galley]]

# Story

[[Dating|3rd Hanomi 1782 IOG]], 05:30 - 15:00

## Morning at the Harbormaster's

The session opens with [[Ellowen]] waking early due to her elven trance. She discovers [[Big Beefy Bob]]'s orange hat is still glowing with a blinding magical light, a side effect of the previous session's events. The house itself is strange: windowless, triangular, and packed with maritime gear. [[Riley]] investigates the clutter and finds a painting of a warship—not a merchant vessel, but a military craft equipped with a siphon and a banner they don't recognize.

The Harbormaster ([[Murotes]]) reveals that [[Aklebe]] is a "ghost of a city" because all trade has been diverted to the capital. In his desperation and boredom, he has gambled away the city's remaining ships. He pleads with the party to go to [[The Panting Shadow]] and win [[The Zoraneset|one]] back. Before they leave, he gives them a stern warning: **"Do not play the cup game."**

## The Streets of Aklebe

As the party heads toward the gambling den, they encounter a homeless man who echoes the Harbormaster's warning, telling them to stay away from the cups. The atmosphere of the city is one of decay and desperation, contrasting with the opulence of the gambling den they are about to enter.

## The Panting Shadow

Inside the den, the party is met by a diverse crowd, including [[Masha]], a firbolg who claims she was "fated" to meet them and quickly attaches herself to the group.

At the bar, an [[Mashop|Oracle]] provides cryptic fortunes. She tells the party they will find prosperity but warns them not to burn anything down. While serving drinks, Ellowen notices the Oracle tapping a rhythmic code on the bar top—a secret communication with the bartender.

## The Gambling and The Apothecary

The party engages in several games to build their pot:

- **Blackjack & Roulette:** Using _Mage Hand_ and _Prestidigitation_, the party manipulates the cards and the dealer to win a significant amount of gold.
- **The Cup Game:** Despite the warnings, the party observes the game, realizing it is a rigged scam intended to drain travelers.
- **The Hand of Fate (Poison Roulette):** The party enters a high-stakes game involving 28 drinks, six of which are poisoned with mugwort. Big Beefy Bob and [[Yvaquis]] take the brunt of the drinking, eventually falling into a groggy, poisoned stupor.

During the games, Ellowen is approached by [[Tabtab]], [[Tukue Potes|the Prince’s]] apothecary. Tabtab, a "catfire" (Tabaxi/Half-Elf hybrid), recognizes Ellowen. She addresses her as "Lady Elowen" and makes specific references to Brackenfall and the Aurelian Keep, nearly exposing Ellowen's noble background to the rest of the party. Riley later attempts to "rizz" Tabtab to steal her diary but fails due to her sharp wit and the Prince's protection.

## Departure

Despite the poisoning and the close calls with their identities, the party wins/buys the [[The Zoraneset|Imperial War Galley]] for 50 gold. The vessel is a massive warship with 60 rowers and a prow designed to shoot Greek Fire. The session ends with the party, including their new companion Masha, boarding the ship and setting sail for the mountains.

# Story Beats

- **Morning at the Harbormaster's**: Ellowen discovers Bob's glowing hat; the party wakes to a pitch-black, windowless house.
- **House Investigation**: Riley discovers a painting of a warship with a cannon, suggesting the Harbormaster has a military or naval background.
- **Harbormaster's Plea**: Murotes explains the economic decline of Aklebe and his own gambling losses.
- **Entering the Den**: The party arrives at "The Panting Shadow" to gamble for a ship.
- **Meeting Masha**: A new ally, Masha, is introduced and identifies Ellowen as "special".
- **High-Stakes Gambling**:
    - **Blackjack**: The party uses magic and sleight of hand to win gold.
    - **Poison Roulette**: The party survives a game involving 28 drinks, six of which were poisoned.
- **Securing the Galley**: The party wins/secures a war galley equipped with a fire-blast prow.
- **Departure**: The party and Masha board the ship to head toward the mountains.

# Characters

- **The Party**
    - **Riley**
    - **Big Beefy Bob**
    - **Ellowen**
    - **Yvaquis**
- **New Allies**
    - **Masha**
- **NPCs**
    - **Murotes** (The Harbormaster)
    - **Tukue Potes** (The Prince, present at the gambling den)
    - **Tabtab** (The Apothecary)
    - **The Dealer**
    - **The Bartender**
    - **The Oracle**
- **Vessels**
    - **The Zoraneset** (bireme dromon, 60 rowers, siphon, ballistae)

---
title: Session 5 - The Zoraneset
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS

# Premise

The party begins their journey aboard [[The Zoraneset]], the bireme Imperial war dromon won in the previous session. As they navigate the open waters toward the mountains, the party must adjust to life at sea, managing a massive crew and a captain with mysterious motives. The voyage is quickly interrupted by a supernatural fog and a harrowing encounter with a vessel, the vessel of the Prince's ship through the fog. Amidst the chaos of naval combat, [[Big Beefy Bob]]’s connection to the "Dead Dreams" deepens, revealing cryptic warnings from a singular, clear voice that identifies itself as the "First Puli."

# Scenes

- [[The Zoraneset]]
    - The Deck (Command and Ballistae stations)
    - The Captain's Cabin
    - The Crew Quarters / Rowers' Deck
	- The Prince's Ship
- The Dream Realm (Dead Dreams)

# Story

[[Dating|3rd Hanomi 1782 IOG]], 15:00 - 25:00

## Life Aboard The Zoraneset

The party familiarizes themselves with [[The Zoraneset]], a 120-foot by 25-foot imperial warship equipped with ballistas and a front-mounted fire siphon. They meet [[Mari Shkari|Captain Mari Shkari]], who informs them that out of a required 200 crew members, they only have 150, meaning the party must step up and assume officer roles.

The party divides the responsibilities:

- [[Masha]] becomes the Ship's Cook
- [[Elowen]] takes on the role of Quartermaster to navigate the ship. Riley secretly hands her a stolen map in the bathroom to aid her checks.
- [[Big Beefy Bob]] is appointed First Mate, tasked with keeping crew morale high. He refuses to take off his glowing orange hat despite the captain's complaints.
- [[Riley]] assumes the role of Bosun, heading below deck to repair holes and broken oars.
- [[Yvaquis]] falls into the role of the ship's Surgeon.

## Masha's Secrets and Royal Slips

While chatting, Masha mentions she is from [[Eivia]] and brings up a missing princess named Evangeline. Yvaquis accidentally responds to the name, heavily hinting to the party that she is the runaway princess.

Later, Mari Shkari tells Masha about a rumour from [[The Panting Shadow|the gambling den]]: black powder was used to blow a hole beneath the [[The Great Palace of Amphos|royal keep]] in [[Amphos]]. The prime suspect was seen wearing a worn, bright woollen cloak and looked like a sheep, a perfect description of Masha, a Firbolg. Despite her nervous demeanour, Masha denies involvement, and Ellowen's insight check fails to glean her true intentions.

## The Water Plane and The Octopus

While on deck, [[The Water Stone|Ellowen's magical stone]] begins to speak to her in a strange voice (jokingly compared to Jar-Jar Binks). It pulls her into a trance where she walks on an endless ocean in the water plane. An indescribable eldritch beast appears, warning her that [[Second Convergence|"The seven have become the six"]] and instructing her to complete [[The Ascension|"the ascension"]] by climbing [[Mount Aemi|the mountain]] in [[Itrea]].

The trance is violently interrupted by the sound of suction as a Giant Octopus attacks the ship. The beast immediately smashes the ship's oars, killing several rowers and dealing massive damage to the hull.

- **Riley** orders the remaining crew to start patching the hull while he fires a flaming arrow—lit by his own magical rock—into the beast's tentacle.
- **Elowen** blasts it with a _Firebolt_.
- **Yvaquis** damages it with her _Divine Spark_ channel divinity.
- **Big Beefy Bob** enters a rage, heavily damaging the octopus with his axes. In a bizarre final blow, Bob attempts to give the terrified octopus a hug while holding his axes, inadvertently executing the creature.

## Ancient Legends and Dead Dreams

That evening, the party eats the octopus, magically flavoured by Ellowen. Captain Mari Shkari shares an ancient legend about a party of seven elementals who travelled the world (including [[Babaren]]), attuned to obelisks, and almost toppled an empire. He warns them that the [[Solara|The Republic of Solara]] used to execute [[Elementals|elementals]], prompting the party to realize the danger of their newly chosen group name, "The Elementals".

The captain assigns night watches, and the party goes to sleep. In his slumber, Big Beefy Bob enters the "Dead Dreams," where a singular, clear voice introduces itself as the "[[Puli Numini|First Puli]].". It promises to help him if he listens. Meanwhile, [[Atiric Texts|a cryptic book]] speaks into Ellowen's mind about the "Bruno walls" and the tearing of the "Margos".

At 4:00 AM, the crewmate [[Dashos]] fails to show up for his watch. At 5:00 AM, the party is jolted awake by a sudden, terrifying male scream, ending the session.

# Story Beats

- **Assuming Command:** The party takes on officer roles to manage the understaffed _Zoraneset_.
- **Masha's Suspicions:** Masha is heavily implicated in a terrorist explosion at the Amphos royal keep.
- **The Royal Secret:** Yvaquis accidentally reacts to her real name, Evangeline Marquis, outing herself to the group.
- **The Trance:** A magical stone pulls Ellowen into the water plane, where an eldritch being warns that "the seven have become the six".
- **The Octopus Attack:** A Giant Octopus attacks the ship, killing rowers and breaking oars before the party slays it.
- **Lore Drop:** The captain recounts a myth of seven ancient elementals who nearly destroyed an empire.
- **The First Puli:** Bob receives a clear, prophetic message in his dreams from an entity offering help.
- **Cliffhanger:** A crewman goes missing, and a male scream echoes across the ship at 5:00 AM.

# Characters

- **The Party**
    - **Riley** (Bosun).
    - **Big Beefy Bob** (First Mate).
    - **Elowen** (Quartermaster).
    - **Yvaquis** (Surgeon).
- **Allies**
    - **Masha** (Cook).
- **NPCs**
    - **Captain Mari Shkari** (The ship's captain)
    - **Dashos** (Crew member)
    - **Hasharus** (Crew member)
    - **The First Puli** (Mysterious dream entity)
- **Enemies**
    - **Giant Octopus**
- **Vessels**
    - **The Zoraneset**

FILE: Campaign 2 - DM Notes\Act 1\Session 7.5 - Riley's Past.md
========================================

---
title: Session 7.5 - Riley's Past
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

# Premise

[[Riley]] is going about on his normal activities in [[Amphos]] when he is suddenly apprehended by the city watch, leased and beat. He was sentenced to execution when suddenly the city guards let him go under orders of the head of the military [[Zenshoran Hagashar]] because "He's not worth it, he's a street rat, there's not enough evidence, everyone said it was a girl half-tabaxi, not a boy."

# Scenes

- **The Zoraneset**
    - **The Lower Deck/Stairs**: Where the Captain’s body was discovered at 05:00 AM.
    - **The Supplies Cabinet**: Found wide open near the murder site, suggesting it was tampered with during the incident.
    - **The Captain’s Quarters**: A focal point of the investigation where tracks and evidence eventually lead.
    - **Crew Bunks**: The location where stolen spirits (alcohol) were used in a botched cleanup of the crime scene.
- **The Port City**: A tiny settlement of approximately 4,000 people where the ship eventually docks.

# Story

[[Dating|1st Ebolumi 1778 IOG - 3rd Ebolumi 1778 IOG]]

### The Crime
1st Ebolumi 1778 IOG, 05:00 - 07:30

[[Campaign 2 - DM Notes/Notable NPCs/Wrensu]] informs Riley that the military are moving an important artifact holding secrets and tells him that he has to make the steal. It is currently stored in the [[The Great Palace of Amphos]], in their archive. He must lift the papers then deliver the message to his merchant contact who will pay him in kind. If Riley askes why him he responds:
> Riley is the courier because he's small, fast, and passes as a girl. He's done it a hundred times.

This time, a City Watch officer intercepts the delivery. Not because they're watching Riley — because they're watching the _recipient_. The recipient bolts. The papers are found on Riley. Riley cannot read these papers because they are written in an old tongue by someone who was very well educated. It appears to be ripped from a memoir of some sort. It is clearly a precious artefact that would belong to the [[Magic Academy of Amphos]] and the [[Head of the Arcane]]. Possession of this is not a theft charge. It is a treason charge. He bolts

This is important because:

- Riley genuinely doesn't know what he was carrying
- He can't explain it without implicating Wrensu
- The Watch has real cause — it isn't just an overzealous arrest
- The sentence of death is proportionate to the crime they believe he committed

### The Arrest
1st Ebolumi 1778 IOG, 08:00 - 08:30

[[Riley]] is on the road between the [[Northern Slums]] market and a contact's house in the lower merchant district. He's in his usual presentation — feminine, small, catlike, invisible. The market is loud. He doesn't notice the two plainclothes officers until they're already either side of him.

Key beats:

- The arrest happens fast — no combat, just numbers and surprise
- They call him "girl" and "cat-girl" during the initial grab. He doesn't correct them.
- The papers are found in the lining of his bag
- He's cuffed in regular iron restraints (he's not known to be an elemental; no suppression cuffs)
- He's taken to the City Watch precinct in the merchant district, not the slums — this is already out of the ordinary

For the player:
Let them attempt escape — one roll. Make it feel possible. Then shut it. There are six officers and a crowded street where running makes you look guilty and being caught running with military papers makes you a spy, not a thief. The Watch wants him alive for now because they want to know who his contacts are.

### Interrorgation
1st Ebolumi 1778 IOG, 10:30 - 29:00

Riley is held overnight. This is where the session slows down and you let the player just _exist_ in the situation.

**The cell:** Stone, damp, one barred window too high to reach. Three other prisoners — a drunk (Barudatos), an old man who doesn't speak (Alibos), and a young woman (Dolashaka) who watches Riley very carefully and eventually says: _"You're not a girl... are you..."_ Not a question. She isn't hostile. She's just been in here long enough to notice.

**The interrogation:** An officer named **Paros Atat** — 40s, tired, bureaucratic, not cruel but not kind — asks how Riley came into possession of the papers, where he was taking them, who pays him. Riley knows nothing useful. He knows Wrensu's name and face and nothing else. Atat doesn't believe him. A man doesn't have to be cruel to apply systematic pressure; Atat just keeps asking.

**DM note on Wrensu:** He knows Riley is taken. His underground contacts told him within two hours. He's trying to get Riley out through back channels — calling in debts, talking to people. But he can't move fast enough and he can't burn his cover doing it. The player doesn't know any of this yet. Let them feel alone.

**The charge:** On the morning of the 2nd, Riley is formally charged. Not theft. Espionage against the Eastern Solaran Empire. The sentence, under Imperial law, is death by public execution in the forum square. The execution is scheduled for the following morning.

### The Night Before
2nd Ebolumi 1778 IOG

This is the session's emotional centre. Riley is moved to a holding cell with three other condemned prisoners. The executions in the morning will be a small batch — seven people, various crimes.
What does Riley do with one night?
Let the player sit with it. Some things you can offer:

- The young woman (Dolashaka) from before is also in this cell. She stole grain from a military storehouse to feed her family. She's been in the system longer than Riley and is grimly calm about it. She's not looking for hope. She asks Riley to tell her something true. ("Not brave. Not 'it'll be alright.' Something true.") — this is a conversation, let it breathe
- A guard brings water. Riley notices the guard's hands are shaking. The guard is young — younger than Riley looks. He doesn't make eye contact. He's more frightened than Riley
- Riley can attempt to pick the lock on his cell. The roll is extremely difficult. If he fails, nothing happens — the guard doesn't notice but the other prisoners watch him. If somehow he succeeds, have him make it two corridors before a different guard stops him cold and brings him back. He gets hit for it. Not badly — a blow to the ribs — but it establishes that escape isn't available tonight.

#### The Flagellation
This doesn't happen at execution dawn. In Imperial procedure, prisoners facing capital charges are flogged on the eve of execution — partly punitive, partly a kind of preparation rite. Twenty-two lashes, administered in the courtyard at second bell of evening. Riley is brought out, strapped to a post, and flogged in front of the other condemned.
Why 22 specifically? Because the officer administering punishment stops at 22 when a runner arrives with a message from the precinct commander. The flogging is interrupted. Riley is cut down and returned to the cell. Nobody explains why.

### The Release
3rd Ebolumi 1778 IOG, 04:00 - 05:30

The executions are due at first light. The other six condemned are taken from the cell. Riley is not. A different officer — older, wearing the uniform of the Tagaminase rather than the City Watch — arrives at the cell. He doesn't introduce himself.

He reads from a document. The language is formal, Imperial Aeikas:
> _Insufficient evidence of wilful participation in espionage. Witness statements describe a girl, half-Tabaxi. The accused is a boy. The accused is released. The accused is a street rat. There is nothing here._

He says the last three sentences not reading from the document. His own addition. He folds the paper. He looks at Riley once — _really_ looks, the kind of look that inventories a person — and then looks away. He gestures for the cell to be unlocked.

On a successful dc10 perception check Riley will spot the officer's sigil: a sun above a crossed blade and scroll. The mark of the Donpotes da Tagaminase's office. If Riley later hears the name [[Zenshoran Hagashar]], he has no reason to connect it to this moment. He doesn't know who the Donpotes is. He's fifteen and he's never had reason to learn.

He's walked to the precinct door and released onto the street. His bag — minus the papers — is returned. His knives are not. His lute is still at home.

### Epilogue
3rd Ebolumi 1778 IOG, 07:00 -

Riley walks home. You can play this as a montage if the player is emotionally tired, or you can walk it beat by beat if they want to decompress.

Wrensu is at the house. He knows Riley is out — his contacts told him before Riley was even on the street. He's sitting at the table with his hands around a cup that has gone cold. When Riley comes through the door, Wrensu doesn't move for a moment. Then he stands up and goes to check the wounds on Riley's back. He doesn't ask what happened in the cell. He doesn't ask about the papers. He works in silence, cleaning the lash marks.

At some point Riley can push for answers. What were those papers? Why did someone with the Tagaminase sigil release him?

Wrensu's answers, and you decide how much to give:

_"The papers were nothing. They weren't mine. I shouldn't have used you."_ — This is a partial lie. They were Wrensu's. He's protecting Riley by claiming otherwise.

_"The Tagaminase? I don't know who intervened."_ — This is also a partial lie. Wrensu doesn't know for certain it was Zenshoran, but he suspects. He has suspected, quietly, for years, that someone in the military apparatus has been keeping Riley off the worst lists. He doesn't know why and he's never wanted to know.

He then says something that he means:

_"You can't be the Freedom Cat anymore. Not the way you've been doing it. They've seen your face now. Find a different way to be yourself."_

He means it. He's frightened. He doesn't say frightened — he says it like an order — but the player should be able to feel what it is.

# Characters

- **The Party**
    - **Riley**
- **NPCs**
    - **Wrensu**
    - **Unnamed Merchant**
    - **City Watch**
    - **Barudatos**
    - **Alibos**
    - **Dolashaka**
    - **Paros Atat**
    - **Officer of the Tagaminase**
    - **Zenshoran Hagashar** (Mentioned only)

FILE: Campaign 2 - DM Notes\Act 1\Session 6 - Murder on The Zoraneset.md
========================================

---
title: Session 6 - Murder on The Zoraneset
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

# Premise

The voyage of **[[The Zoraneset]]** turns into a nightmare as the crew discovers the brutal murder of their leader, **Captain [[Mari Shkari]]**. The session is a high-stakes investigation as the party navigates a ship full of suspects, contradictory evidence, and a crew on the brink of mutiny. The mystery deepens with signs of a calculated clean-up and clues pointing toward **[[Dashos]]**, a crew member who had previously gone missing from his watch.

# Scenes

- **The Zoraneset**
    - **The Lower Deck/Stairs**: Where the Captain’s body was discovered at 05:00 AM.
    - **The Supplies Cabinet**: Found wide open near the murder site, suggesting it was tampered with during the incident.
    - **The Captain’s Quarters**: A focal point of the investigation where tracks and evidence eventually lead.
    - **Crew Bunks**: The location where stolen spirits (alcohol) were used in a botched cleanup of the crime scene.
- **The Port City**: A tiny settlement of approximately 4,000 people where the ship eventually docks.

# Story

[[Dating|4th Hanomi 1782 IOG]], 05:00 - 11:00

### Discovery of the Captain's Body

The session begins at 05:00 AM with a scream that alerts the party. **[[Ellowen]]**, following a **Natural 20** perception check, discovers the body of **Captain Mari Shkari** on the other side of the stairs. The scene is gruesome; the Captain is "bleeding very much," and his body appears to have been dragged. **[[Masha]]** is found nearby with blood on her right arm, claiming she had just found him, though **[[Riley]]** is initially skeptical of her innocence.

### Forensic Clues and the Cleanup

The investigation reveals several strange details about the murder:

- **The Alcohol Cleanup**: A crew member discovers his strong spirits have been stolen and partially spilled on his bed. The party finds that the Captain's body smells strongly of these spirits, suggesting the killer attempted to wash the body or the floor to hide the scent of blood.
- **The Open Cabinet**: A supply cabinet that was previously locked was found open near the stairs.
- **The Murder Weapon**: The wounds consist of multiple slits and hacks. A knife is eventually found with a name on it, though its direct connection to the killing is debated.
- **The Scent Trail**: A successful check allows the party to follow a scent of blood and alcohol that leads directly toward the **Captain's chambers**, implying the killer may have come from or fled to that area.

### Suspects and Motives

| Supsect       | Motives                                                                          |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Big Beefy Bob | Insulted his little Orange Bowler Hat                                            |
| Riley         | Victim attempted to woo him and flirted with him                                 |
| Ellowen       | Said Thumpwick was not allowed to eat out of the supplies                        |
| Yvaquis       | Made her stop smoking and confiscated her herbs                                  |
| Masha         | Disrespected her goddess and faith and threatened to reveal her bomb-plot secret |
| Dashos        | Stole his alcohol while on watch                                                 |
| Hasharus      | Insulted his puppy and was also told his puppy could not eat from the supplies   |

The primary suspect emerges as **Dashos**, the crew member who failed to show up for his 4:00 AM watch in the previous session.

- **Dashos's Actions**: Witnesses report seeing Dashos dragging the Captain out of his bed around 04:30.
- **Motive**: The party discusses potential motives, including the Captain's previous harsh discipline and his recent conflict with **[[Big Beefy Bob]]** over his refusal to remove his orange hat.
- **Riley's Daggers**: Riley's own silver daggers are examined to see if they match the wounds, adding to the internal tension of the group.

#### Clues

| Hour  | Rota                         |
| ----- | ---------------------------- |
| 01:00 | Yvaquis, Mashageta           |
| 02:00 | Big Beefy Bob, Ellowen       |
| 03:00 | Mari Shkari, Riley, Hasharus |
| 04:00 | Dashos, Ellowen              |
1. Thumpwick and the puppy are gleefully raiding supplies together
2. Hasharus is still under the impression that alcohol is banned while on duty. He has not been told otherwise
3. Dashos seems happier today
4. Dashos smells of herbs
5. Dashos' breath smells of alcohol
6. Dashos has a little green hat
7. Yvaquis is the only one who brought herbs on the ship
8. Dashos is missing his knife to cut ropes
9. [[Pupolas Crate|The puppy]] remembers being told “_stay_” that night if someone could speak with animals
10. The puppy is weary of Riley
11. [[Mari Shkari]] has got the wrong holy votive next to his bedroll, instead of the god Salumi the patron deity of [[Solaum]], he has Nari the god of War
12. Dashos is a devotee of [[Nari|the cult of War]] in Amphos
13. There is a spilled bottle from Hasharus's personal collection near Dashos's bed
14. There are crushed herb remains near the mast on the top deck, directly below the crows nest
15. Dashos's hat and clothes seem new or recently cleaned, they look immaculate
16. The puppy didn't bark last night

### Arrival at Pithertara

As the party attempts to maintain order, the crew is in a state of panic and mutual suspicion. **Big Beefy Bob** continues to experience disturbing "Dead Dreams" and hearing supernatural voices, which are becoming noticeable to his companions. The session concludes as the ship pulls into a small port city of 4,000 people, leaving the party to decide to hand over the suspect (Dashos) to local authorities after placing him under citizens' arrest. Big Beefy Bob concludes that it was indeed Dashos that killed Mari Shkari, hands him over. The city guards and members of the [[Tagaminase]] come over and arrest [[Masha]], leading to her death by beheading as she fought for her escape.

# Characters

- **The Party**
    - **Riley**: Instrumental in searching for the murder weapon and managing the crew.
    - **Big Beefy Bob**: The focus of the Captain’s recent ire; continues hearing the "First Puli" in his dreams.
    - **Ellowen**: Discovered the body; conducted the critical forensic checks.
    - **[[Yvaquis]]**: Performed medical examinations to confirm the Captain's death.
- **NPCs**
    - **Captain Mari Shkari**: The victim; found murdered and cleaned with alcohol.
    - **Dashos**: The prime suspect; seen dragging the Captain shortly before the body was found.
    - **Masha**: Found with blood on her arm; suspect turned witness.
    - **Husharis**: Another crew member present during the discovery.
