FILE: Campaign 2 - DM Notes\Act 1\Session 5.5 & 6.5 - The Story of John Iron Chest.md
========================================

---
title: Session 5.5 & 6.5 - The Story of John Iron Chest
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

This is the story of how John Ironchest joined the party of the Elementals and discovered he is the power elemental. He begins at his mountain home and makes his way south through mountains, forests, towns, villages and rivers to arrive at [[Pithetara]]. This is where he participates in a [[World Bodybuilding Order|WBO]] competition and gets spotted by the elementals in the crowd.

# Session 5.5
[[Dating|3rd Hanomi 1782 IOG]], 06:00 - 17:00
## Premise

In session 5.5 in his cave home he is met by a WBO envoy, [[Leofric Wordbear]], where he is handed a [[John Ironchest's Letter|letter]]. 

## Scenes

- **John’s Mountain Cave Home**
- **Arrival of the WBO Envoy**
- **Preparing to Leave the Cave**
- **Waterfall Exit from the Cave**
- **Mountain Pass Challenge by Oswin Truegrip**
- **Ravine Descent and Farewell to Leofric**
- **Discovery of the Power Stone**
- **Forest Clearing with the Golden Tree and Stone Circle**
- **Vision from the Central Stone**
- **Elemental Vision at the Tree Circle**
- **Collection of Tree and Stone Samples**
- **Night Camp and Trap**
- **Encounter with the Hooded Figure**
- **Departure from the Forest**
- **Arrival in Akrossa**

## Story

[[John Ironchest]] stands in the middle of his mountain cave home, in the Duchy of [[Dornsia]], north of the [[Eastern Solaran Empire]], honing his body through lifting rocks and fighting his training dummy, wondering what is next in his life. He sees his bonded great-axe to his left, standing perfectly sharpened and maintained against a boulder, surrounded by broken pottery and numerous broken awards from the [[World Bodybuilding Order]] (WBO). As the World's Strongest Man he feels no more competition or spark in his life as he watches the day go by with each drip in the central stream of his home. This is where he bathes, eats, sleeps, fishes and he feels like his meaning with each passing second, still he is immensely proud of all he's done. He stares out to the waterfall at the end of the cave, where the entrance and exit lies, and ponders just what is left for him to do. There is no more challenge left, no more grind left to fight. He has truly beaten the grindstone.

Next walks in an envoy, announcing his entrance, yet humbling himself before John. He claims he is from the WBO and that his name is [[Leofric Wordbear]] and he is here to give John an important message from the council of strongermen. With this notification he hands John a [[John Ironchest's Letter|letter]] detailing that he is due in [[Pithertara]] for the next WBO competition. Happy to receive this information John is excited, yet he also is aware he's won before he even steps foot on to the stage ahead of him, and is more underwhelmed than he expected. He knows there is no real competition here but instead a slaughter. He has already reached the peak that man-kind has to offer.

Leofric recites the words of the letter to John.

John begins to pack his belongings, but leaves his axe behind as he has no use for such trivial things as weapons when his body is perfect. He does not believe a well-formed human has need for such exterior works. Once packed, he equips his scale-mail bracers to match his scale-mail thong and moves forward. The only problem is he has to leap through the waterfall ahead, not wanting to lose his bronzing oil he casts minor illusion on himself so for the time he is past the waterfall he still looks perfectly bronzed when in reality his bronzer has come off of his body. This astounds the envoy who asks for his particular bronzing oil in the future for his personal use.

While walking along the narrow mountain pass down to the bottom of the ravine, another bodybuilder approaches John announcing his name, [[Oswin Truegrip]], and that he will beat him here and now, taking his place at the competition in Pithertara and asserting his place as the new World's Strongest Man, going so far as announcing that he will be the strongest man across all the planes. John turns to him as the man boldly announces his moves before striking, stuff like "Fingerspear" and "Strikes of Fury". John gets fed up of Oswin always coming up short before clapping and the compressed air pushes Oswin over the edge, disabling him at the bottom of the ravine for good.

Once down in the ravine, Leofric tells John what is to come on his journey to Pithertara, saying that he will brave mountainous terrain, forests, strange people and rivers to get to his destination, but not to be deterred. Well, John wasn't deterred in the slightest and acknowledged what he said and moved on with haste. Leofric said his goodbyes and headed back to the World Bodybuilding Order's HQ.

John just before leaving the mountains and entering the forest south, is intrigued by one particular [[Power Stone|rock]]. He does not recognise this and wonders as to why it glows in the colour of Tyre (in the real world). A purple most striking and one that can not be made cheaply, and a colour not typical of rocks, at least certainly not in the area he is in. It does not appear carved nor natural to him. As soon as he picks up the rock he feels revitalised and his muscles appear much stronger than that of his normal body. The rock instantly attaches itself to his thong, like a codpiece and reshapes itself. Almost netting and weaving itself into the scale-mail. Confused but accepting of the new rock, he continues on his path southward.

He now enters a forest and finds a mysterious clearing on his left. As he enters he finds a golden tree and a small stone circle. Within the stone circle is a centre stone that appears to have veins of purple.

As he interacts with the centre stone he sees visions, in reverse, of events that transpired with the other travelling party from [[Session 6 - Murder on The Zoraneset|the murder aboard The Zoraneset]], to the burning of [[Riley's House]] and [[Session 1 - The Stones in Amphos|the heist of the other stones]], but not before that.

As he interacts with the tree he is placed in the other tree circle on the [[Amphos-Aklebe Road]], but to him the area appears as a tar-dark void, a place of nothingness and a place without meaning. He perceives the interactions each party member has with the other golden tree as manifestations of their elemental being. He sees a body made of flames touch him and cause him harm through burns; a maiden of water touch the floor by him and dissolve into water and appear on the opposite side and record her findings; a person of Earth illuminate the void and feel the world beneath her; a ghostly, dark figure run up to him hug him and then back away confused. He also sees a spirit of wind float around a strange place, this one was clearly not in the same place as the others. Finally he sees a world full of electricity but no soul bound to it.

After he believes he has gathered enough information he notices as he touches the tree he also becomes stronger, he takes a shaving of it and stores it in a jar, as well as a shaving of the centre stone.

Once he is satisfied he sets up a rudimentary trap and sleeps. In his sleep a hooded figure in white and gold sets off the trap. John awakes, but as he does the hooded figure disappears, as though he was never there, leaving nowt but a note in his place saying "You must join them. Climb." John saw just enough of the figure to make out his emerald eyes and boots.

John is confused but moves on to his next destination in the morning. He finally arrives in [[Akrossa]].

## Story Beats

- **John Ironchest** trains in his mountain cave home in the **Duchy of Dornsia**, north of the **Eastern Solaran Empire**, lifting rocks and fighting a training dummy.
- John reflects on his life as the **World’s Strongest Man** under the **World Bodybuilding Order (WBO)** and feels he has no remaining challenges.
- He observes his perfectly maintained great-axe but chooses not to carry it, believing his body alone is sufficient.
- A WBO envoy named **Leofric Wordbear** arrives with a message from the council of strongermen.
- Leofric delivers a letter summoning John to compete at the next WBO competition in **Pithertara**.
- John prepares for departure, equipping his armour and leaving his axe behind.
- While exiting the cave through a waterfall, John uses **Minor Illusion** to maintain the appearance of his bronzing oil.
- During his descent from the mountains, another bodybuilder named **Oswin Truegrip** challenges him for the title of World’s Strongest Man.
- John defeats Oswin effortlessly by clapping, generating a shockwave that knocks him off a ravine.
- At the base of the mountain, Leofric warns John about the long and difficult journey ahead.
- John continues south toward the forests.
- John discovers a mysterious **Power Stone**, glowing purple.
- When he picks up the stone, it fuses into his scale-mail thong and greatly enhances his strength.
- John discovers a **golden tree and stone circle** within a forest clearing.
- Interacting with the central stone gives him **reverse visions** of events connected to the murder aboard **Murder on The Zoraneset**, the burning of **Riley's House**, and the theft of other stones.
- Touching the golden tree places John in a **void-like vision** of another tree circle on the **Amphos-Aklebe Road**.
- In the vision he observes manifestations of elemental beings representing another adventuring party interacting with the tree.
- John collects **shavings of the golden tree and the central stone** for study.
- He sets a rudimentary trap and sleeps in the clearing.
- During the night a mysterious **hooded figure in white and gold** triggers the trap and leaves a note reading: _“You must join them. Climb.”_
- John briefly notices the figure’s **emerald eyes and boots** before they vanish.
- The following morning John continues his journey.
- John arrives in **Akrossa**, leading into the events of the main story.

## Characters

- **John Ironchest**
- [[World Bodybuilding Order]]
	- [[Leofric Wordbear]]
	- [[Oswin Truegrip]]
- Border Guard
- Hooded Figure in the Woods

# Session 6.5
[[Dating|4th Hanomi 1782 IOG]]

## Premise

John Ironchest, a travelling strongman and competitor of the World Bodybuilding Order, departs the town of Akrossa on a journey to reach a competition in Pithertara. Along the way he acquires a powerful warhorse, hires a young orphan named Ulriki as his squire, and demonstrates extraordinary physical strength to overcome practical obstacles. Travelling through settlements including Byblarascu and Pyrma, John encounters religious institutions, suspicious villagers, wilderness threats, and logistical challenges. After recovering a stranded riverboat and navigating hazards along the river, John ultimately reaches Pithertara just in time to enter the bodybuilding competition. The story establishes John’s character as a sceptical, physically dominant traveller navigating a world shaped by remnants of Solari civilisation, while forming the beginnings of a partnership with his new squire.

## Scenes

- [[Akrossa]]
    - Tavern
    - Stable
    - Tannery and Leatherworks
- Road between Akrossa and [[Byblarascu]]
- Byblarascu
	- City Gates
	- Temple of Harakishi
- Road between Byblarascu and [[Pyrma]]
- Pyrma
	- Boat in River
- Boat
	- Chain-Breaker Bandits
	- Sunken Aqueduct
	- Shipwreck
- Pithertara
	- Docks
	- Tavern
	- Stables
	- WBO stage

## Story

### Leaving Akrossa
06:00 - 08:00

[[John Ironchest|John]] wakes up in a tavern built into the ruins of an old Solari granary. The city of 1,254 is waking up; the smell of roasting chickpeas and damp river fog fills the air.

John makes his way downstairs talks to the tavern-keep, who laments that the grain that is stored outside is too heavy to move (400kg/barrel), and that the horses next door at the stables keep eating the grain out of the barrels when they inevitably break. John takes up the task of moving the barrels, he carries all 5 at once, moving 2Mg of grain at once. The tavern-keep was impressed by this show of strength and skill he compliments John saying he could hang off his arms. John remembers that the horses are at the stables and asks the tavern-keep if he could take a horse, the tavern-keep wants the horse off his hands and allows the purchase. There are 5 horses for sale:

- [[The Black Hare]]
- Silverboat
- Akrossa's Bottom Fist
- Ordinary Day
- Army's Call

After observing all the horses, John deduces that Come-At-Me White was the strongest and largest horse. The tavern-keep says he used to work for the [[Imperial Army of the Eastern Solaran Empire|Imperial Army of Amphos]] and that the horse was sired from an imperial war-horse. Come-At-Me White is a 4 year old, very dark bay, stallion, weighing approximately 550 kg, and stands at 17 hands high; he has a narrow white blaze. He selects this horse to be his and the tavern keeper says to have him with no payment, he also purchases some grain to carry with him to feed the stallion.

When saddling the horse he discovers the saddle doesn't fit and that the reins, bridle and bits are also too small with the mouse-piece causing the stallion extreme discomfort, hurting the horses mouth and face.

He goes back to the tavern-keep after undressing the horse and queries if there is a leather-worker or tannery in the city. The tavern-keep indulges John with the information required, saying that the leather-worker used to work for the imperial army and has retired to here. John makes haste to the leather-worker.

The leather-worker, [[Basil Ceyx]], confirms that he worked as a leather-worker for the Imperial East Solari army, making armour and leather items for the cataphracts. He claims he works with the finest leather and uses the finest tanning techniques and finest metals. He examines the saddle, and other fittings for the horse and says the fittings were made for a much smaller mare, not at all 17 hands tall and weighing much under 500kg. Saying he will need to create brand new fittings, but not to fret as he will make them in under 25 minutes as he is extremely skilled, it will only cost John 40 gold. John argues this is expensive and that the [[World Bodybuilding Order|WBO]] is the perfect place to advertise this saddle. Basil says he is already offering a discount and is rushing, the price should have been 50 gold. John says he will give a personal endorsement at his next show in [[Pithertara]], a city of 8158 people, if he pays just 20 gold. Basil accepts 21 gold, making it at a loss as he understands that John must have it and he expects a massive endorsement, also making him a leather sponsor patch. When inspecting it even John, an untrained eye, can see this is saddle is of exceptional quality, made in the imperial style. 

John goes to leave and when passing the square gets approached by [[Ulriki|a young, impoverished, malnourished lad]]. To John he looks 12 years old. As he approached the man on the horse he begged for food and bread. John asks the young man where his family was and if he has any parents, the young man says they are poor and live in the slums. John tells the young man to follow him and goes to the tavern where he buys the kid a meal and chats with him. John asks the tavern keep who says he recognises the boy as poor and a beggar but does not know his name nor where he came from, apparently he appeared here a couple months ago. John then proceeds to interrogate the young boy discovering he is from [[Lqlima]], has no parents, no money and no job opportunities. John takes pity upon the boy and offers him a job for 2 silver pieces per day as his squire before even discovering his name. The boy notices this and tells him his name is *Ulriki*, a [[Setting/Cultures/Solari|Solari]] name, but John is unbeknownst to this fact. 

John sets off, still sceptical of the boy and clutches his possessions closely, and mounts his horse and saddle, he also sets his squire on the horse, bareback.

#### Akrossa to Byblarascu
08:00 - 09:30

While trotting along the path, the horse is alerted to the rhythmic thump of a beast hopping across the path ahead, John sets the horse to a gallop and avoids being encountered by a Giant Toad. Which crosses the path behind them unawares.

### Byblarascu
09:30 - 10:30

John approaches the gates of the city and talks to the guard who directs him to the temple of [[Harakishi]] in the city and explains he is the patron god of the city. John is not impressed by this as he sees the god as a proxy of strength but not as a representation of pure, unfiltered, internal strength.  

He goes to the temple anyway to receive a blessing for his weak squire, Ulriki. Ulriki receives the blessing then feels much better, energised and more confident. He becomes a devotee of Harakishi.

A priest notices John's extreme strength and gives him holy water in return for blessing the local guard's practice weapons. John refuses but takes the holy water anyway as he does not believe in Harakishi and does not understand the fascination with magic and the divine.

He also heard form Ulriki about the pillar in the city square. He asks the priest about this who tells him it is a replica of the [[Obelisk of Origin]] in the Eternal City of [[Solaum]]. He learns that here the Obelisk of Origin is called the Obelisk of Power.

Pleased with this information he proceeds to remount his horse with his squire, and make way to Pyrma.

#### Byblarascu to Pyrma
10:30 - 11:00

The road narrows and becomes overgrown. John notices that he is being stalked by at least 1 Scouts. He again asks Come-At-Me White to gallop and out paces the scouts.

### Pyrma
11:00 - 12:00

John arrives in [[Pyrma]] with his small travelling band and is immediately met with suspicion by the local residents. Ulriki shares this feeling and also states that he has been here before on his travels stating that "The first time I was here, everyone was unwelcoming and suspicious of me as I travelled through here. I left as soon as I came." Ulriki explains that it is severely undeveloped and only has a population of 50.

The village headman is approached by John who for a boat. The headman laughs and retorts:
	"we only have one and it's stuck!"
	"It's in the Reeds of the Weeping Woman. Everyone who goes there ends up crying and returning."

John must navigate the local politics. The villagers believe the boat is cursed. He has one hour to gather supplies (oars, pitch, rope) before heading to the water.

#### Recover the Boat

The boat is wedged in a thicket of razor-grass and mangrove roots.

John finds this laughable and leaps 30ft across the river. He lands just short of the boat where he is attacked. A *Mud Mephit* has made a nest in the hull. He launches the creature into the river where the fast current carries it away.

John passed the mephit with ease and wondered what everyone was making a fuss about.

He attempts to pull it out using the anchor. The chain for the anchor snaps due to rust and deterioration from being stuck for so long without maintenance.

After clearing it with help from the village people, who Ulriki brought along to help after some socialisation with the farmer, John dry docks the boat by pulling it to shore; acting as an anchor, he allows Come-At-Me White, Ulriki and the anyone who wants passage to Pithertara to board. He then pulls the boat out to the river and hastens the journey by pulling it most of the way.

### Boat Trip to Pithertara
12:00 - 13:30


#### 1. The Toll of the Chain-Breakers

A group of river bandits has stretched a thick, rusted iron chain just beneath the water's surface between two Solari-era bridge ruins.

- **The Conflict:** As the boat hits the chain, the player must make a **DC 13 Dexterity saving throw** to avoid being tossed overboard.
- The bandits fire crossbows from the ruins.
- John Ironchest intimidates them and drives them away

#### 2. The "Sunken Arch" Obstacle

The river narrows at a collapsed Byzantine aqueduct. The 345 m³/s discharge creates a "white water" effect, forcing the boat toward a jagged stone pillar.

- This is a "Skill Challenge." The player needs to navigate the boat.
- John failed to avoid the pillar and gives in.
- John hangs self over boat to tank the aqueduct pillar, ready to beat the pillar and save the ship
- Ulkiri steers boat of the way of the pillar.

#### 3. The Cargo Retrieval

The player spots a half-sunken, razed Byzantine transport boat wedged against a sandbar. A survivor is clinging to a crate.

- The current is moving at 18 km/h relative to the shore. Once the player passes the wreck, they can't easily row back up-stream.
- John leaps from the boat once in range, throws the survivor and grabs the rope attached to the crate and leaps before the boat passes the wreck.
- The victim compliments John Ironchest and gives him a **potion of healing**, and allows him to take the crate which contains rum, some spell scrolls, some herbs, as well as some googly eyes, it also contains a [[Manuscript on Tabaxi|torn copy of a manuscript about the history of tabaxi]].

### Arrival at Pithertara
John, on the anchorless cog borrowed from the hamlet of Pyrma, arrived in Pithertara, he sailed down the river to the mouth and docked at the harbour. This is where he heard news about [[The Zoraneset]] and someone being killed and someone else being arrested. As he only had 15 minutes to make it to the WBO competition, he ran across the city, dropped off his belongings, stabled his horse and bought a room in an inn for both him and Ulriki. He then registered his attendance at the competition and walked onto the stage.

## Story Beats

- John Ironchest awakens in a tavern built inside the ruins of a former Solari granary in the city of Akrossa (population 1,254).
- The tavern-keep complains that grain barrels stored outside are extremely heavy (~400 kg each) and frequently broken by horses at the neighbouring stables.
- John moves all five grain barrels simultaneously (~2 Mg total), impressing the tavern-keep.
- John purchases a horse from the tavern-keep’s stable. Available horses:
	- Come-At-Me White
	- Silverboat
	- Akrossa's Bottom Fist
	- Ordinary Day
	- Army's Call
- John selects Come-At-Me White, a 4-year-old dark bay stallion (~550 kg, 17 hands) with a narrow white blaze.
- The tavern-keep reveals prior service with the Imperial Army of Amphos, stating the horse descends from an imperial warhorse.
- The horse is given to John without payment; he purchases grain to feed it.
- While saddling, John discovers the saddle and fittings are sized for a much smaller horse and cause significant discomfort.
- The tavern-keep directs John to a local leather-worker.
- John visits **Basil Ceyx**, a retired leather-worker formerly employed by the **Imperial East Solari Army**, who produced armour and leather equipment for cataphracts.
- Basil confirms the saddle was made for a smaller mare.
- He offers to craft **new saddle and fittings in ~25 minutes** using imperial techniques.
- Initial price: **40 gold** (reduced from 50 due to rushed work).
- John negotiates by offering a **public endorsement at the next WBO competition in Pithertara**.
- Final agreement: **21 gold** plus Basil producing a sponsor patch.
- Finished saddle is of **exceptional imperial-style quality**.
- While leaving the square, John is approached by a **malnourished boy (~12 years old)** begging for food.
- The boy claims:
    - No parents
    - No work or money
- John purchases a meal for the boy at the tavern.
- The tavern-keep confirms the boy appeared in the city several months earlier but is otherwise unknown.
- John offers him employment as a **squire for 2 silver pieces per day**.
- The boy reveals his name: **Ulriki** (a **Solari name**, though John does not recognise this).
- John departs Akrossa with Ulriki riding bareback behind him.
- While travelling the road, **Come-At-Me White senses danger**.
- A **Giant Toad** crosses the path.
- John avoids the encounter by galloping past before the creature notices them.
- At the city gate, a guard directs John to the **Temple of Harakishi**, patron deity of the city.
- John views Harakishi as a **symbol of strength but not of true internal strength**.
- John nonetheless brings Ulriki to the temple to receive a blessing.
- Ulriki receives the blessing and becomes **energised and devoted to Harakishi**.
- A priest notices John’s strength and offers **holy water** in exchange for blessing local guard weapons.
- John refuses the request but **takes the holy water regardless**, expressing scepticism toward divine magic.
- Ulriki informs John about a **pillar in the city square**.
- A priest explains it is a **replica of the Obelisk of Origin** from **Solaum**, locally called the **Obelisk of Power**.
- John departs for Pyrma.
- The road becomes narrow and overgrown.
- John detects that **scouts are tracking them**.
- He outruns them by galloping.
- John arrives at **Pyrma**, a small hamlet (~50 people).
- The residents are suspicious of outsiders.
- Ulriki reports similar hostility from a previous visit.
- John seeks a boat to travel downriver.
- The **village headman**, explains the village’s only boat is stuck in the **Reeds of the Weeping Woman**.
- Villagers believe the area is cursed.
- John prepares supplies (rope, pitch, oars).
- The boat is located **wedged in razor-grass and mangrove roots**.
- John jumps ~30 ft across the river to reach it.
- A **Mud Mephit** nesting in the hull attacks.
- John throws the creature into the river where the current carries it away.
- Attempting to free the boat, the **rusted anchor chain snaps**.
- With assistance from villagers gathered by Ulriki, John frees the boat and drags it ashore.
- The vessel is loaded with passengers including Ulriki and **Come-At-Me White**.
- John pulls the boat into the current and **tows it downriver manually**.
- River bandits stretch an iron chain beneath the water between ruins.
- Boat collision risks throwing passengers overboard.
- John avoids combat through intimidation
- Collapsed aqueduct creates whitewater currents.
- Boat must navigate a dangerous pillar.
- John hangs self over boat to tank the aqueduct pillar, Ulkiri steers boat of the way of the pillar.
- A half-sunken, burned transport boat is spotted against a sandbar.
- A survivor clings to a crate.
- The survivor rewards John to the contents of the crate:
	- Potion of healing
	- Rum
	- Herbs
	- Spell scrolls
	- A **torn manuscript: _The History of Tabaxi_**
	- googly eyes
- John arrives at Pithertara using the borrowed cog from Pyrma.
- At the docks he hears rumours concerning the Zoraneset, including a killing and an arrest.
- With only **15 minutes before the WBO competition**, John:
    - Stables Come-At-Me White
    - Secures lodging for himself and Ulriki
    - Drops off his belongings
    - Registers for the **World Bodybuilding Order competition**
- John proceeds directly to the stage.

## Characters

- **[[John Ironchest]]**
	- [[The Black Hare]]
	- [[Ulriki]]
- [[Akrossa]]
	- The Tavernkeep
	- [[Basil Ceyx]]
- [[Byblarascu]]
	- Gate Guard
	- Temple Priest of Harakishi
- [[Pyrma]]
	- Farmer
	- Other residents
	- Headman of Pyrma
- River Bandits
- River Survivor

FILE: Campaign 2 - DM Notes\Act 1\Session 9 - The Shallows Remember.md
========================================

---
title: Session 9 - The Shallows Remember
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

[[Dating|6th Hanomi 1782 IOG]]

## Story

### Life on the Zoraneset (6th Hanomi, 06:00–14:00)

The session opens with the ship a day out of Pithertara. Give the table a breath before the combat — let the players establish their routines, their relationships with the reduced crew, the texture of being at sea.

_[[Riley]]_ — The bosun's job is below deck: oars, hull integrity, crew morale among the rowers. There's a rower named **[[Peles]]**, seventeen years old, who has started following Riley around with unconcealed admiration. He's from a coastal village the party will visit at the end of the session, though he doesn't mention it yet. He's nervous about approaching the southern shipping lanes and won't say why.

_[[Ellowen]]_ — The [[Atiric Texts]] spoke to her again last night. The session opens with the stone repeatedly talking about Water. Just the word. Over and over, a voice like pressure at depth: _ami, ami, ami_ — which is the Solari word for water, and more specifically the [[Water|water element]]. She can tell the party or not. The Quartermaster's charts show they're approaching a stretch of coast marked in old Imperial notation as _Moli Ithami_ — the Itami Sea's inner waters.

_[[Big Beefy Bob]]_ — First Mate's job: crew morale and discipline. Two rowers got into a fight overnight over rations. One of them says the sea smells wrong today. The other agrees, which is why they fought — neither wanted to say it first. Bob can investigate: a successful Perception or Nature check (DC 12) confirms it. The water around the ship is unusually clear. No fish. Not one.

_[[Yvaquis]]_ — As ship's surgeon she has been tending three rowers with lash wounds from the previous captain's regime. One of them, **Toras**, an older man, grew up on the Itami coast. If she builds rapport with him (any social roll, DC 10), he'll tell her: _"This stretch. The Shallows of Ithami. My grandfather said the deep things here have moods. Last year the fishing boats stopped coming back. Not all of them — just enough."_

_[[John Ironchest]]_ — He's been running a physical conditioning programme for the undermanned crew. During the morning exercise John notices [[The Black Hare]] is distressed in his below-deck stabling — pacing, refusing water. Horses are good barometers.

**[[Woubble]]** can be wherever seems funniest. [[Pupolas Crate]] has, inexplicably, befriended the ship's cat, which is a narrative problem for the ship's cat.

---

### The Warning (6th Hanomi, 14:00–14:30)

Give the players this in two beats, five minutes apart.

**Beat one:** One of the rowers on the port side shouts. Something just touched his oar from below. Not hit — _touched_. Deliberately, like a hand. He pulls his oar in. The stroke falters. Ellowen, on the quarterdeck, can see over the gunwale into the water and with a DC 12 Perception check makes out shapes below the surface. Many shapes. Moving with the ship.

**Beat two:** A figure rises from the water at the port bow and clings to the hull. It's a merfolk — but wrong. The eyes are clouded, a flat grey-white that should be dark. The gills are working too fast. The hands gripping the ship's timbers are bleeding from the clench. It opens its mouth and produces a sound that is almost language — the [[Ephe]] traders who sometimes put in at [[Amphos]] use a clicking coastal dialect — but fractured, repeating the same syllable: _a broken word, looping, like a scratch on stone._

It does not attack. It is looking at the ship with those ruined eyes and it is terrified.

Then six more emerge behind it, and they are not terrified. They are furious.

---

### COMBAT — Attack in the Shallows (14:30–16:30)

**Design philosophy:** This is a ship combat, not a dungeon encounter. Think in terms of three simultaneous problems rather than one monster to kill. Players are spread across a 120-foot vessel with 120 panicking crew. Their individual actions matter but so do their decisions about where to be and what to order.

#### The three simultaneous problems

##### PROBLEM 1: THE HULL BREACH 
_Relevant: Riley, Yvaquis, any crew directed below_

Merfolk are using bone spikes and coral tools to attack the hull below the waterline at two points. They're not strong enough to sink the ship quickly, but they will compromise the oar ports and flood the lower rowing deck within 20 minutes without intervention.

Below decks: two breach points, one on each side, each requiring a DC 14 Strength check to brace with timber and pitch, or a DC 12 Dexterity check to jam with emergency materials. Two successes total plug the breaches. Failure on any one check means the flooding accelerates — reduce remaining time by 5 minutes. Yvaquis can direct rowers with a DC 13 Medicine/Athletics hybrid (she knows which men are strong enough, she's been treating them). Riley can use his Thieves' Tools to jury-rig a brace, DC 12.

The merfolk attacking the hull: four of them. They are not coming aboard. They are working, fast and focused, like sappers at a wall. They will fight if fought but their goal is the breach, not the crew.

##### PROBLEM 2: THE BOARDING
 _Relevant: Big Beefy Bob, John Ironchest, crew_
 
Twelve merfolk have pulled themselves over the gunwales onto the main deck. They are attacking rowers — specifically targeting the oarsmen, not the officers. They want the ship dead in the water. If they take out enough rowers, [[The Zoraneset]] cannot manoeuvre away from the shallows, and she'll eventually be driven onto the rocks by the current.

**Stat block — Frenzied Merfolk (modified):** Use standard Merfolk stats (MM p.218) with the following changes: advantage on attack rolls while within 5 feet of another merfolk, but disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws. They will not retreat. They will fight until unconscious. The grey-white eyes glow faintly when they're hit hard — not with light, but with something like heat.

Bob as First Mate can use his action to direct crew (DC 12 Persuasion/Intimidation) — on a success, four crew members take coordinated attacks against one merfolk this round, each with +3 to hit for 1d6 bludgeoning. On a failure, two crew members are overwhelmed and need rescuing next round.

John Ironchest on an open deck against twelve merfolk is, frankly, in his element. Let him be terrifying. The Power Stone should pulse when he hits one — they react to it. One merfolk stops its attack on a rower and turns to face John directly with something that looks, briefly, like recognition.

---

##### PROBLEM 3: THE BALLISTAS AND THE SIPHON
_Relevant: Ellowen, any player who takes the quarterdeck_

The Zoraneset has two ballistas on the aft deck and the fire siphon at the prow. Someone needs to direct these, because the crew at the ballistas are trained gunners but they've never fired on merfolk at close range on their own ship — they're waiting for an officer to make the call.

**The fire siphon** is devastating. It can clear a 30-foot cone of burning naphtha, dealing 3d8 fire damage (DC 13 Dex save for half) to everything in the area, including the ship. A player at the prow can fire it — but they will need to be careful about where the crew are standing. Used well, one blast ends Problem 2. Used carelessly, the party will be putting out fires on their own ship.

**The ballistas** are better for Problem 1 — a bolt fired into the water beside the hull will scatter the merfolk working on the breach. Each requires a ranged attack roll (+5 to hit) against AC 12 (underwater targets). Hit: 3d10 piercing, kills one, scatters the others (they lose one breach action next round).

**Ellowen's Water Stone:** The stone has been growing warm since the shapes appeared under the water. If Ellowen uses a spell while holding it this combat, there's a side effect: the clouded eyes of the merfolk nearest her _clear_ for one second. Not all of them. Just the ones nearest her. She should notice this.

---

#### The Leader — Shaleth

At the midpoint of the combat (after roughly 6 rounds, or when two of the three problems have been addressed), something larger surfaces astern.

**Shaleth** is a merfolk elder — if merfolk can age, she is old. She is not grey-eyed. Her eyes are clear, dark blue, and she looks at the party with intelligence and fury and something underneath both that might be desperation. She carries a staff of deepwater coral wrapped in what appears to be kelp but is, on close inspection, woven script — the same clicking language, made visible.

She does not attack. She surfaces and she _watches_.

If a player attempts to communicate (any language, DC 15 — DC 10 if Ellowen uses the Water Stone, which seems to help), Shaleth can produce three words of Solari, heavily accented: _"Stone. It. Hurts."_

She means the elemental disturbance. She cannot explain it. She doesn't have the language. But the party now has a data point: the merfolk attack isn't aggression. It's pain, and the pain is connected to the elements.

Shaleth retreats when the combat ends or when the party clearly attempts communication over combat. The grey-eyed merfolk, without her presence, lose cohesion — they don't retreat cleanly, they just... stop pressing. Some slip back into the sea. Some need to be restrained or finished. The party makes their own calls.

---

### Aftermath (16:30–18:00)

**Damage report:** The DM should decide the hull damage based on how well Problem 1 was managed. If it was addressed quickly: superficial damage, no speed penalty. If it went badly: one oar bank is flooded, speed halved until repaired. Repair requires putting in to shore — which is actually useful, because that's where they're going.

**Rower casualties:** Two to four rowers are badly hurt (unconscious, overboard, or dead) depending on how Problem 2 went. The crew's morale takes a hit. The crew who were saved by player intervention are visibly grateful. Peles, the young rower who grew up near the end-of-session settlement, is one of the survivors if the players fought well — let them notice that.

**The first merfolk they saw** — the terrified one with the clouded eyes who arrived first and did not attack — is still clinging to the port hull. When the combat ends, it is still there. It is trembling. If anyone reaches down to it, it flinches but doesn't release its grip. It has been holding on to the ship this entire time. It doesn't look dangerous. It looks exhausted.

What the players do with this creature is their choice. It cannot communicate beyond emotional expression. If they bring it aboard, Woubble attempts to befriend it immediately, which is a good tone-break after a hard combat. It will be important later.

**Bob's Dead Dreams note:** If Bob rests during the voyage later, the First Puli has something to say about what just happened — something about the sea having a long memory and elements having weight.

### Arrival - Myrneleu (7th Hanomi, 08:00)

The ship makes the coast by dawn the following morning, driven by necessity (hull damage, wounded crew, exhausted rowers) and by Ellowen's charts showing a small settlement on the next navigable stretch of shore.

**Myrneleu:**

Population 1985. A former Imperial provincial harbour — you can see the bones of what it was in the quayside stonework, the crumbling customs house, the grid of streets that was once wider. The Imperial design had capacity for 12,000. What remains uses maybe a third of that infrastructure, the rest colonised by goats, sea grass, and enterprising families who've knocked through walls to make compound living.

The economy: fishing, small-scale trade with the river settlements inland, and a dwindling timber trade from the forested hills behind the town. They used to export salt. The salt trade stopped eight months ago when the merfolk started attacking the salt beds at the shallow coast.

**The Archon:** Myrneleu is governed by **Archon Vaela Murso** — a woman in her late fifties, former Imperial customs administrator, now the de facto head of a settlement that has been bleeding people to merfolk attacks for eight months. She is not panicking. She is past panicking and into the cold management of ongoing disaster. When the Zoraneset pulls into her harbour, she is at the dock in person.

She has questions before she has welcome: _Who are you? Where from? What happened to your hull? Did you come through the Shallows of Ithami?_

When she hears they came through the Shallows and survived and have a merfolk on board, she pauses for a long moment and then says: _"You'd better come in."_

---

### Myrneleu — Key Locations & Encounters

**The Harbourmaster's Hall** (former customs house, now town hall): Vaela spreads charts on the table. Eight months ago, the merfolk were a neutral presence — they sometimes traded shells and deep-water materials with the fishing boats, a non-verbal but functional relationship. Then something changed. The attacks began at the new moon. The salt workers were first. Then the fishing boats. Two weeks ago, a merfolk came ashore at night — not to attack, but to _look_ at the town. The night watch found it standing in the market square at third bell, staring at the Solari-era monument in the centre (a broken column with an inscription nobody can fully read anymore). It didn't attack. It left at dawn.

Vaela wants the attacks to stop. She does not know why they started. She does not have the resources to fight back — the town guard is twelve people. She has been hoping the problem would solve itself. It has not.

**The Monument:** The broken column in the market square. If any player investigates (DC 13 Arcana or History), the inscription is Imperial Solari, archaic register, partial: _"...the element of the sea requires no monument, as it builds its own."_ The column was erected during the reign of [[Aelius|Puli Ailushi Libisai]] It is 1032 years old. Something has scratched at the base of it recently. The scratches are not random. They are the same clicking script pattern from Shaleth's staff.

**Peles:** The young rower leads the players to his family here. His mother, **Demi**, runs the only functioning inn (three rooms, communal table, genuinely excellent fish stew). She recognises the situation with the merfolk from old stories her grandmother told — "when the sea holds a grievance, it isn't against _us_, it's against something _in_ the water." She doesn't know what that means in practical terms, but she's been trying to tell Vaela for months and Vaela is not a stories person.

**The Salt Beds:** A short walk along the coastal path, the former salt production area. Shallow evaporation pools, currently abandoned. At low tide, the bottom of the pools is visible and covered in coral-scratch writing — much more extensive than the monument. The merfolk have been writing here. Extensively. Whatever they're trying to communicate, this is where they've been trying to communicate it. It needs translation.

**The Merfolk Aboard the Zoraneset:** If the party brought the grey-eyed merfolk with them, it becomes animated when it sees the town. Not aggressive — urgent. It tries to move toward the salt beds. If allowed, it leads the party there, presses its hands into the writing on the pool floor, and looks at them with those clouded eyes. The clouds in its eyes, in direct sunlight, are not grey. They are faintly yellow. The same yellow as the disrupted electricity element.

### The Revelation

This session doesn't deliver the answer — it delivers enough pieces that the party can assemble a hypothesis:

The merfolk in the Shallows of Ithami are experiencing something analogous to what Ellowen experienced in the water plane — an elemental disturbance radiating from... somewhere nearby. The salt beds are on a ley line. The monument is on the same ley line. The Shallows of Ithami are on the edge of it.

The merfolk aren't attacking because they're hostile. They're attacking because the elemental disruption is causing something like madness — the grey-white eyes are the symptom — and they can feel that it's coming from the direction of the ships passing through. They can't distinguish between the source and the vessels near it. The attacks are, in their way, a desperate attempt to stop something they can't describe.

What's causing the disruption is not in Myrneleu. It's further East. Toward Itrea. Toward Mount Aemi.

Vaela will provision the ship and let them use her drydock for basic hull repairs if they can either explain the merfolk situation in terms she finds credible, or make concrete progress on stopping the attacks. She doesn't need the attacks ended tonight. She needs someone who understands what's happening — she's been operating in the dark for eight months. That's enough.

### End

Two possible endings depending on time and energy:

**Hard stop:** The party has made port, met Vaela, seen the salt beds, and has enough to discuss. End on the image of Peles showing Ellowen the scratch writing in the salt beds at low tide, the sun going down behind the hills, and the sound of Myrneleu going quiet for the first time in months — because, for one night, the sea is calm.

**Soft ending with a hook:** As the party settles into the inn for the night, Vaela mentions, almost as an aside, that a traveller came through Myrneleu three weeks ago — _"strange person, older than they looked, asked a great many questions about the old column, left before dawn, didn't pay for the room"_ — and left something: a single line of Solari written on the table of the room they occupied, which Demi kept because it seemed important. The note reads: _"The column remembers. Ask it what it saw before you climb."_

No signature. Ellowen's Water Stone is warm against her hand.

---

## Notes

**Shaleth:** She shouldn't be killed if it can be helped. She should be available for future contact if the party wants it. She is the one coherent intelligence in the merfolk situation and she will remember the ship that tried to talk.

**The Electricity connection:** The yellow in the grey-eyed merfolk's eyes is a deliberate plant — the destroyed Electricity element is leaving traces in beings sensitive to the elemental world. Don't confirm this. Let it sit.

**Rhoda:** Myrneleu's oldest fisherman, if anyone talks to him, says he once saw a creature that was half person and half something else, flying low over the water at dawn, near the outer reef. _"Sang something. Changed the wind. Then gone."_ That's your plant.

**The merfolk aboard:** If they kept the grey-eyed merfolk, it should go back to the sea when the ship enters harbour — slipping over the side quietly, without drama. If anyone watches it go, it pauses in the water and looks back once, and the clouds in its eyes are almost entirely gone.

To [[Alaric Aurelian Vale]], Duke of [[Brackenfall]], and to the House that bears his name,

The Sun moves, and the world follows.  
Know that the [[Solara|Empire of the Solari]] is attentive to its borders, and mindful of those houses whose blood has long stood between order and shadow. The Vale has endured because it has understood this truth.  
By the same understanding, I now set forth what has already been measured, weighed, and found consonant with the will of Heaven.  
Your daughter, [[Ellowen|Lady Ellowen Aurelian Vale]], is named to stand beside my son, [[Tukue Potes|Prince Tukue of House Potes]], Koronuganamon, and marked from birth for the continuance of the ancient imperial line of great Solari emperors.  
Lady Ellowen is therefore acknowledged as betrothed to the Prince of the Solari and shall be received in due season as Princess-Consort of the Solari, her person and issue thereafter bound to the great, ancient, Solari imperial law, protection, and destiny.  
The House of Aurelian Vale is, by this union, drawn from the Empire’s edge into its blood. Its lands shall stand under the Sun’s regard. Its name shall be spoken among kin. Its future shall be ordered and it shall evermore be protected by the [[Imperial Army of the Eastern Solaran Empire|Tagaminase]].  
The rites of union shall be observed during High Summer, at the Festival of the [[Unconquered Sun]], within the [[Solar Basilica of Amphos]], temple to the pantheon, where emperors are crowned and time is kept. Preparations are already underway, as is fitting.  
[[Solaris Vanguard|The Vanguard]] will arrive when the season turns and will escort her thusly. They will not announce themselves twice.  
You will return your sealed affirmation before the sun completes its next great turning, that all things may proceed without disturbance and the Empire may remain whole in its course.  
As has been decreed by the great god [[Solaum (god)|Solaum]] of [[Solaum|the great city]] and the Solari Empire who has given us his blessing for our future, and let the great god [[Nari]], god of war, be absent from our futures.

From [[Bardashes|Bardashes]], Koronuganamon, Mag Hirag ta Puli Solari.

teaken yourself in Pithertara after-ovest. No hoose is needed on your swithly behalf. Your Set is known.

ebb, if you must.

Leofric Wordbear

*\[All dashes are burnt off or omitted pieces of text\]*
# On the - origin and - dispositio- people- taba-

A compendium of Traveller’s accounts, Imperial records, diplomatic correspondence and scholarly conjecture.

Compiled by praetor-historian _Kallisthenos Haemi of the bureau of Imperial Records in Amphos of the Empire of Solara_

_Commissioned under the reign of Bardashes in_ _1779 IOG_

## Preface – To the Reader of the C-endium

It - come to the attention of the bureau of Imperial Records in Amphos, record keepers of the Empire of Solara, that the peoples that are styled as _tabaxi_, called by the scholarly people of Linhua of the Divine Empire of Daxing in the far east as the Tao-baxi, and by the western lands as the Tarakshi, remain the subject of considerable ignorance within the borders of the Solaran Empire and indeed all of Shul and Ararukoi. This ignorance is not merely an affront to the dignity of scholarship; it is a practical hazard for those engaged in matters of trade, diplomacy, or intelligence who may find themselves in the company of such persons without the least preparation for what to expect of them.

The bureau has therefore charged the present writer with the task of compiling, from all available sources, a coherent account of the Tabaxi people: their place of origin, their customs, their capacities, and the circumstances by which they have arrived, in such negligible numbers, upon the shores and borders of our empire. This work draws upon the records of the First Embassy to Daxing, which was conducted in the year 918 after the founding of the great city; upon the private correspondence of several merchants who have travelled the silk-laden roads of the continent of As; upon a single first-hand testimony from a tabaxi individual resident within the empire, the only known full tabaxi according to census records; and upon the frankly unreliable but occasionally illuminating accounts preserved in the popular literature of Amphos.

The reader is cautioned that the tabaxi of the realms to the far east are not the tabaxi of rumour, nor are they servants of demonic forces, they do not steal children, and their eyes do not see in pitch tar darkness with the precision of a sniper archer from Eivia, though their low-light sight is considerably better than that of the human. They are persons, entirely complex and unique, various between individuals of the species and largely indifferent to the mythos surrounding their disposition that shul has constructed around their existence, or lack thereof on the lands.

With the preamble concluded, may the words speak from the pages, as the words of Atiri were said to have done in the distant past.

Kallisthenos Haemi – Amphos, 3rd Hanomi, 1779 IO-

  

# Section II – On their Origin and Homeland

There is a claim that the Tabaxi of the east descended from creatures from before known creation, that must be concluded to be false for we know that we can intermingle among them without judgement, no creature known to man has ever come from before creation by the gods above, may Shuzi be grand beyond all. For we know that as per the legends of the Aeia and the scholars of old tradition claim that all peoples of all lands descend from the Aeia at the foot of Mount Aemi. We know the aeia are the original inhabitors of the land. Whether the tabaxi fall under this or represent some unique separate branch is not a question the writer wishes to adjudicate, having neither the theological prowess, authority or patience for such arguments.

What can be stated with confidence and certainty is this: The tabaxi are native to the lands of the east, in particular to the territories of Divine Empire of Daxing, whose capital of Lilinlu is at least six months of travel by even the most efficient means of transportation from the eastern frontier of the empire. The first formal record of contact between our world and theirs is the embassy dispatched in 918 IOG by the Solari emperor of that era to the court of Emperor Liuxian of Daxing. The linhua scholars of the imperial court recorded this embassy in detail. They make no mention of tabaxi in their records indicative of either their absence or the lack of remark on the existence of the tabaxi by the Solari mission in 918 IOG.

In contrast, the Linhua records of the same period refer to Tabaxi with apparent and evident familiarity. They appear in marginalia of various ledgers, manuscripts and other papercrafts as carriers and merchants of specific goods, spices, dyes, and a resinous incense the Daxing call xian-ho meaning roughly “heart-fire” in translation, along the overland and overseas routes further east of Daxing itself, of which there are few. The linhua do not treat the tabaxi with fascination or as a curiosity to be studied. This strongly implies that the Tabaxi are considered either native to the land or have -ded there for long enough -onsidered native -ved that even in th -e Tabaxi a- further east from - our mer- know of, but of w-

\- those lands the hearsay is consistent on several points. - climate is warm, forested, volatile and the land mountainous and islanded. The people live in city-states and war-bands of moderate sizes, no great empires exist, but all pledge allegiance to a central power or war lord. They have no professional armies however and are instead levied with skilled knights between, these have a special name and control land within the islands. They trade extensively with the Daxing but resist subservience to the divine realm.

## On Their Physical Character

The Tabaxi are a humanoid people of generally human stature, though tending toward the taller end of human variation. Their most immediately apparent characteristic is their feline morphology: they possess pointed ears set high on the skull, vertical pupils that expand dramatically in low light, retractile claws of limited but functional sharpness, and in many cases a tail of modest length, though this last feature varies considerably between individuals. Their skin is covered in a fine, short fur whose colouration follows the patterns of the great cats — spotted, striped, or solid — in a range from near-white to near-black. Their facial structure is recognisably humanoid, with a slightly lengthened jaw and prominent cheekbones, giving the face a quality that western observers frequently describe as "beautiful in a way that is not quite right."

The half-Tabaxi — that is, persons of Tabaxi and human parentage, or Tabaxi and elven parentage — are a distinct matter that the present writer treats separately in Section V. The blending of Tabaxi traits with those of other races produces results that are, in the experience of every observer consulted for this work, wholly unpredictable. The inheritance does not follow the orderly patterns that a physician might expect. A half-Tabaxi may inherit the ears and claws and none of the colouration, or the colouration and none of the eyes, or some configuration the parents themselves could not have anticipated. The only feature that appears with near-universal consistency in half-Tabaxi individuals is the ears of a cat.

  

# **SECTION III** **—** **On Their Distribution in the Empire and the West**

The Tabaxi are, by any measure, extraordinarily rare in the Empire of solara and in all of Shul. The Bureau’s census of 1770 IOG recorded Two individuals of Tabaxi or part-Tabaxi descent within the city of Amphos itself, this of course does not include the slums; the figure for all territories of the empire combined is estimated at fewer than 10 individuals, though the Bureau acknowledges that this figure is unreliable for reasons elaborated below.

The difficulty of counting them is, in part, a consequence of their rarity creating discrimination. A Tabaxi in Amphos is immediately identifiable. They cannot pass unseen in a market crowd. This visibility, in a city with an institutional memory of Elemental persecution and a broad cultural tendency to treat the foreign-born as lesser, means that Tabaxi residents of the city have strong motivation to avoid official enumeration. The Bureau’s census-takers reported considerable resistance in the lower districts of the city, where it is known that at least one resident with tabaxi heritage is known to exist, and it is the present writer’s opinion that the true number is perhaps half the recorded figure due to extermination of the creatures in underdeveloped land.

How did they come to be here at all? Several pathways can be identified with confidence.

The first and most historically significant is the overland trade route through the eastern steppe of As. The great trade routes that once connected Solara to Daxing passed through As in their entirety, and Tabaxi merchants and their families were a documented presence on those routes from at least 1200 IOG onward. Some remained in the western cities where the routes terminated. Others were stranded by the disruptions of the Freiburg Migration Period, finding themselves in a world where the routes that would have carried them home no longer functioned. Their descendants remain.

The second pathway is less dignified: enslavement. The Solari Republic, in its later centuries of expansion and persecutio- swept broadly in its definition of who might be legally enslaved. Elemental persecution provided legal cover for -vement of anyone the authorities chose to classify -tal, and the appearance of - Tabaxi — visibly alie- rare enough to have no political advocates, far from any homeland that might seek their return — made them vulnerable to exactly this mechanism. The Bureau’s records from the late Republican period and the early Empire contain a number of legal proceedings in which Tabaxi were accused of elemental affinity on evidence that reads, to the modern eye, as wholly fabricated. These persons were in practice enslaved under cover of law.

It would be dishonest to present this history as fully concluded. The present writer cannot state with confidence that no Tabaxi individual within the Despotate currently lives in conditions of illegal servitude. The Bureau’s writ does not extend to every household in the lower districts of Amphos, and the capacity of private individuals to obscure such arrangements is not inconsiderable.

  

# SECTION V – On the Half-Tabaxi Races

A full-blooded Tabaxi in Amphos is exotic; their foreignness is so complete as to inspire a certain cautious deference in some quarters, in the manner that any very unfamiliar thing may forestall easy contempt. The half-Tabaxi inspires no such deference. They are sufficiently familiar to be placed on a social scale, and their placement on that scale tends, in the experience of every observer this work consulted, to be low. They are regarded by those of full human or elven descent as impure. They are regarded, in some cases, by full-blooded Tabaxi as diluted. They are also, crucially, identifiable at a glance as different — which, in a city where being identifiably different has historically carried legal risk, is not an abstract disadvantage.

The half-Tabaxi lifespan appears to fall to that of the human norms, though the evidence for this is limited and the variance between individuals is considerable. Their physical capabilities exceed the human average in certain respects — reaction time, agility, visual acuity at range and in low light — while not extending to the more extreme capacities attributed to full-blooded Tabaxi in popular legend. A half-Tabaxi will not outrun a horse. They will, however, almost certainly outrun you.

the Bureau’s position, as established by the Ruling of Bardashpotes, is that half-Tabaxi born within the territory of Solara are to be treated as full citizens under Imperial law, entitled to all protections thereof. Whether this ruling is observed in practice by local magistrates and the City Watch is a question the Bureau cannot answer in this forum without giving offence to persons above the present writer’s station. The reader may draw their own conclusions.

  

# SECTION VI — - Appearance in the Historic-

This section reproduc - f commentary, those entries in the Imperial historical -n which Tabaxi individuals appear by name or description. The list is not long. That is itself a piece of evidence about how this Empire has treated persons who did not fit its categories.

## The Slave Market Records of Itrea

The city of Itrea — holy city-state, ancient seat of the Aeia tradition, acquired by Solara in the eastern conquests of the 500s IOG — maintained unusually detailed slave market records as a function of its administrative character. These records, preserved in part in the Bureau’s archives, include a number of entries for individuals described as “cat-servants” in the old Republican tongue. The present writer does not know whether these were Tabaxi, half-Tabaxi, or individuals of some entirely different description whose feline characteristics were noted by the record-keeper. Given the rarity of Tabaxi in the western lands even in the height of the Republic, the present writer judges the majority to have been the latter. But the records show that persons of visibly non-human appearance were trafficked through Itrea’s slave markets with some regularity, categorised by their appearance, and sold without any record of their names or origins.

The irony is not lost on the present writer that Itrea — holy city, place of pilgrimage, city where the great philosopher Atiri himself was enslaved — was also a market for persons classified by their bodies as less than persons.

## The Merchant Accounts from As, 1200–1400 IOG

The surviving merchant accounts from the period of the great overland trade routes through As contain approximately forty references to Tabaxi individuals by name. Of these, twelve are identifiable as the same individual across multiple accounts — a merchant called, in various transliterations, Tzeshiran, Tze-shira, or simply “the Cat of the Eastern Road.” Tzeshiran appears to have operated a trading concern specialising in dyes and medicinal resins between Daxing and the eastern cities of the empire for a period of at least forty years. Multiple account-writers comment on the longevity of the operation and attribute it to either supernatural means or "an uncanny memory for prices and faces that no human merchant could match." Whether Tzeshiran was Tabaxi or half-Tabaxi, male or female, is inconsistently reported across the accounts, which the present writer takes as evidence that western merchants were either genuinely unable to determine these characteristics or found them unimportant to record.

The Testimony of Aboridas Makosi, 1763 IOG

The most recent first-hand testimony in the Bureau’s possession comes from a guardsman named Aboridas Makosi, who submitted a report to the City Watch of Amphos in 1763 IOG regarding a disturbance in the lower districts involving, as he recorded it, "a young half-tabaxi who could not have been more than a couple days old, Was placed alone in a barn in the slums, without any indication of parentage or provenance." The child was left with no regard for health, nor other means of survival, the report ends here. There is no record of what became of the child. The Bureau has been unable to locate any subsequent documentation. This section reproduces, with brief commentary, those entries in the Imperial historical record in which Tabaxi individuals appear by name or description. The list is not long. That is itself a piece of evidence about how this Empire has treated persons who did not fit its categories.

He goes on to talk of another disturbance from the prestigious pleasure district in Amphos where a young catfire, no older than 16 was sold to the Royal palace as an apothecary. He has no further documentation or details of the catfire.
