---
title: Varma's Memoirs
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

I have been told, by more people than I can now count, that I should write things down. That memory is unreliable. That the past deserves a witness. These are arguments made by people who have not yet understood that the past does not ~~care whether it is witnessed~~ — or rather: the past does not need a witness. It needs to be let go.

I am writing this anyway. Not because I have changed my opinion on the matter. Because I have been alive long enough to know that the things we refuse to do eventually do themselves, whether we sanction them or not.

I do not know what year it is as I begin. I have not counted years in a very long time. The [[Setting/Cultures/Solari|Solari]] have their [[Dating|calendar]] now — thirteen months, twenty-eight days, anchored to the second resettlement of [[Solaum|a city]] on a river where my people once held court. I find I cannot bring myself to use it. There is something obscene about measuring the world’s age from the moment humans arrived at a place we had already abandoned.

That is an unkind thought. I will leave it.

――――――――――――

# i. the earliest things I am willing to put into words

I was not the oldest of us. I should say that first, because I have noticed that people assume it, and the assumption irritates me in ways I cannot fully justify. Sere was older. Miranu was older. Several others I will not name here, because to name them is to use up the last of them, and I am not ready to do that.

What I can say is that I was old enough to remember before [[The Convergence]]. Before the gods decided that the arrangement was no longer working and took their leave of it. I was old enough to have had opinions about whether they should.

I will not record those opinions here. They are still too sharp.

What the world was like before, I have been asked this by every curious student I have ever had, and I always give the same insufficient answer: fuller. That is the honest word for it. The world was fuller. Magic was not something you reached for; it was something you swam in. Every stone had weight that was not merely physical. Every tree had a voice that was not merely wind. The great cats of the eastern forest could hold a conversation with you if you were patient and they were in the mood, which they rarely were. The sky at night was not dark. It was lit from within by the movement of things that no longer move.

I am aware that this description sounds like the nostalgia of the very old. It probably is. But I have lived long enough on both sides of the Convergence to know that nostalgia, in this case, is simply accurate memory.

I wrote “never return to this” next to this passage the last time I read it. I am returning to it anyway. Some instructions are not worth following.

We were not gods. I want to be clear about that, because the records — what survive of them, filtered through six or seven generations of Chinese-whisper scholarship — tend to describe my race as divine or semi-divine, and this is not accurate. We were old, and we were capable of things that other peoples were not, and we moved between layers of the world that most beings cannot perceive. None of that is divinity. Divinity is something else. Divinity is what the gods had, and what they took with them, and what left a hole in the world when they ascended that nothing has fully filled since.

We served them. That is the honest way to say it. We served as intermediaries between the divine and the mortal, between the celestial currents and the physical plane, between the things that could not speak to each other directly and needed someone in between. Diplomats, the language of this age would say. Translators.

We were very good at it. And then the gods decided they no longer needed translators. And then we were no longer necessary. And then ~~and then the betrayal~~. ~~and then what they did to the Courts~~. ~~and then Miranu, and Sere, and the others I will not name~~.

I will come back to that. Or I will not. I have not decided.

――――――――――――

# ii. the long middle, which is most of it

After the Convergence, I walked.

That is a simple sentence for an enormous span of time. I walked for longer than most civilisations have existed. I watched the peoples of this world emerge from the rubble of the pre-Convergence order — blinking, confused, reaching for a magic that no longer answered them, building fires because fire at least still worked. I watched [[Ebbu]] go up on the sand. I watched the first quarried stones of [[Itrea]] settle into the hillside. I watched children who had no word for what I was decide what word to use and arrive, inevitably, at some version of ghost.

I was not a ghost. I was a survivor. The distinction felt important at the time. It feels less important now.

I did not teach in those centuries. I did not want students. A student requires you to believe that what you know is worth passing on, and I was not convinced of that. I had spent an age passing things between the divine and the mortal and the celestial, and the result was: the gods left, my people were killed, and the world stripped itself of magic like a man pulling off a burning coat. I was not certain that my accumulated knowledge was an asset rather than a record of catastrophic failure.

I walked, and I observed, and I did not intervene. I watched the [[Qatha]] develop their calendar. I watched the long dark after the Convergence do its patient work of erasure. I watched the new peoples build their new stories about what the world had been and why it was now the way it was, and I noted, with what I chose to call scholarly detachment, how rarely the stories bore much resemblance to what I had actually seen.

At some point I stopped being angry about this. That was probably the most significant moment of the long middle period, and there was no one to witness it.

I walked past [[Solaum]] four times before it existed. Past the [[Atri]] River bend, past the stone that would later be the foundation of the [[Obelisk of Origin|Obelisk]] that housed the [[Power]] Element. I always found the site unsettled. Something in the ground there. Not corrupted — I would not use that word. Waiting.

There was a period, I will not say when, because the dates mean nothing to me and the specifics are private, when I tried to end it. Not in the sense that you might fear. I am not easily ended, and I knew it. But I made a serious effort to find whatever passes, for something like me, for a natural conclusion. I climbed the mountain. I sat in the highest silence. I waited for whatever had taken Miranu and Sere to come and take me.

It did not come.

I came back down the mountain. I decided, in the absence of any alternative, to find something to do with the time.

――――――――――――

# iii. the boy

I found him by accident, which is how the important things tend to arrive.

He was burning down a forest. Or beginning to. A small fire that had the ambition of a large one, feeding on itself with the particular enthusiasm of magic that has just discovered it exists. I could feel it from a considerable distance — not the heat, but the shape of it. The mana around him was rearranging itself in real time, folding toward a point that would, if left alone, either consume him or consume the forest or both.

He was sitting in the middle of it with his hands out, watching. Not afraid.

Watching.

That was the thing that stopped me. I have seen many people discover their elemental capacity for the first time. Terror is the usual response, or grief, or denial. He was watching it the way you watch a flame you have never seen before — with total, hungry attention. As if the most urgent thing in the world was to understand what it was doing and why.

I told him he was imbalancing the forest. He did not look up. He said, without turning: “I know. Tell me how to stop.”

Not “help me stop”. Not “can you stop it”. “tell me how.”

I had been alive for longer than I could accurately count, and in all of that time no one had ever made me want to laugh with that quality of involuntary, helpless, genuine surprise.

I named him Aetor. The One Who Knows. It was forward of me — a name is a promise, and I had not yet decided I was going to teach him anything. But the name came out before I could reconsider it, and he, and his people, softened it to [[Atiri]], and that was that. The name made the promise real.

I poured everything into him. That is the only honest way to say it. Forty-five years of teaching that was not merely instruction but evacuation — I was emptying myself of what I carried because I had finally found someone I trusted to carry it further. Every technique I had retained from before the Convergence. Every fragment of knowledge about the elements that the [[Aeia]] tradition had partially preserved and partially mangled. The old draconic tongues. The nature-magic that sings rather than commands. And the elemental arts, which are both simpler and more dangerous than any of the others, because they do not require you to reach outside yourself.

He was a difficult student. I want to say this. He argued with everything. He demanded justification for every rule. He wanted to understand the mechanism of each technique before he would consent to practise it, which is not how you learn to handle fire; you learn to handle fire by handling fire; you learn the mechanism afterward, when your hands have stopped shaking. We had this argument approximately three hundred times. He was wrong about the method. He was right about the underlying principle. I never admitted this to him while he was alive.

That last line is a lie. I admitted it on a night near the end, when I had begun to understand that the end was coming. He pretended not to hear me. He was merciful that way.

He could not feel [[Aushuzi]]. I want to record this separately because it troubled him, and because his interpretation of it — that the goddess did not come to him because he was too mortal, or too damaged, or somehow rejected — was wrong in a way I did not know how to correct without telling him things I had decided not to tell him.

Aushuzi did not come to him because Aushuzi, by the time Atiri was climbing that mountain, was a pattern in the architecture of the world rather than an entity capable of arrival. The gods did not withdraw to a place from which they might return. They became something else. What the Aeia tradition preserves as contact with the divine is, in the most honest analysis I can make, contact with the residue of divinity — the impression left by a foot that has long since lifted from the ground. I could feel it because I was tuned to the original, because I had spent my entire existence as an instrument calibrated to hear a note that is no longer played. Atiri could not feel it because there was nothing to feel.

I could not tell him this. He needed to believe the mountain held something. And in the way that mattered most — the way that made him keep climbing, keep asking, keep

wanting — it did.

The mountain taught him humility and endurance and loneliness and truth. Those are real things. They do not require a goddess to be real.

――――――――――――

# iv. what I knew was coming

I knew before he did. I think I had known for several years before the end — that the teaching was concluding, that what I had to give was mostly given, that the shape of what came next was not going to include me standing in the forest calling him back to practice at dawn.

I did not tell him. This was deliberate and I stand by it, and I expect he would disagree if he could read this, and he would be partially right. But a teacher who tells a student “I am leaving soon” changes what the student learns in the time remaining. The last lessons become about the leaving rather than the work. I did not want that. I wanted the work to stay the work until the last possible moment.

What I gave him in those final years without naming them as final:

Everything I knew about the elements as they had been before the Convergence — not the diminished, post-Convergence version that the world had settled into, but the original, which is deeper and stranger and considerably more dangerous.

The nature of the Elemental Shards, and what the Obelisks are, and why they were built, and what lives inside them. The Aeia preserved the knowledge of how to build the containment. They did not preserve the knowledge of what they were containing or why. I gave him that.

The Convergence cycle. The interval. What the third one will require and why it will require it. This I gave him in the form of [[Atiric Texts|the Texts]] themselves — not as explicit instruction but woven through everything, so that the right reader at the right time would find it waiting. Atiri did not know he was recording it. He thought he was writing memoir.

A name. Not his. Not mine.

I will not put it here.

On the morning of the fifteenth of Narimi, I woke before him. I sat with the forest for a long time. I said the things that need to be said to the things that remember them.

Then I left.

I did not leave a body because I do not leave bodies. I did not leave a note because what I had to say was already in his hands, in the Texts, where it would wait as long as it needed to wait. I did not say goodbye because goodbye is a promise that the one leaving will be missed, and I did not want him to grieve what was not a death.

He searched for forty days. I watched him search for forty days. This was perhaps unkind. I am not certain I made the right decision. I am certain that if I had let him find me, he would not have gone to Solaum and built [[Atiri Centre of Magical Excellence|the school]], and everything that needed to follow from that would not have followed.

The school needed to exist. The Texts needed to be in a place where they would be found and hidden and found again.

Forty days of grief was the price. I paid it for him, watching from a distance, which is its own kind of cost.

――――――――――――

# v. after

I have kept moving. That is the substance of everything after Atiri. I have kept moving, and I have watched, and I have made certain adjustments to the world’s arrangement when the adjustments were small enough to make without tipping into the kind of intervention that changes the nature of what I am trying to do.

The Texts have been lost three times and found four times. Twice I found them myself and moved them. The first time I cursed them with a spell that prevents it from opening except under the control of a Fire Elemental. The second I charmed them with a spell that will speak to the possessor so long as they are an elemental.  Once they were moved by someone else and I followed to make sure they ended up somewhere appropriate. The appropriate place changes depending on what is needed next. They are not meant to be a permanent archive. They are meant to be a delivery mechanism, and delivery mechanisms need to be in the right hands at the right moment, not in a vault where they will be preserved and ignored.

I watched [[Solara|the Empire]] rise. I watched [[Aelius]] make himself Emperor, which was the most extraordinary act of practical ambition I had seen in a thousand years, and I had seen considerable ambition in a thousand years. He was correct that it needed to happen. He was correct about most things, which I found irritating and also moving. He did not know about the cycle. He did not need to.

I watched the Empire fall, which took longer and was less dramatic than the rise, as falls usually are. [[1127 IOG - 1330 IOG - Freiburg Migration Period|The Migration Period]] looks catastrophic in retrospect; it felt, from the inside, like a slow tide that no one could find the will to turn back. The peoples involved were not villains. They were cold and hungry and moving toward warmth and food. The empire they dismantled had been built on practices that did not deserve permanence. The world that emerged was not better, precisely, but it was different, and different was what the Convergence cycle required.

There is a version of this paragraph that acknowledges my own culpability more directly. I wrote it. I burned it. I will not re-examine it here. If you are reading this and you know which specific events I am declining to discuss, you already know enough about them to make your own judgment, and your judgment does not require my assistance.

[[Stormshroud Legion|The Stormshroud]]. The decline of Solaum. The slow forgetting of everything the Republic had preserved of the old knowledge, which was itself only a fraction of what the Aeia had preserved, which was itself only a fraction of what existed before the Convergence. Each generation loses a little more. This is not entropy; it is preparation. A world that retained full memory of the previous Convergence would approach the next one with strategies and expectations that would make it worse. The forgetting is part of the mechanism.

I repeat this to myself as necessary. It has not yet stopped working entirely.

――――――――――――

# vi. on the stones, briefly, because I find I cannot write at length about them

The stones are not my creation. I want to say that clearly because there is a version of events — I have heard fragments of it in the scholarship that has developed around the Convergence history — that implies that we, or more closely *I*, made the elemental artifacts. We did not make them. The Convergence made them. We understood them, which is different.

What I understand about them:

Each stone is a shard of what the relevant element was before it was diminished. Not a container. A remnant. The stone and the element are the same thing at different scales.

A stone does not choose its bearer. The stone and the bearer are in a relationship of resonance, not selection. When a stone finds the person whose elemental nature matches the frequency of the remnant, there is no choosing involved. It is like asking whether a bell chooses its note.

The [[Electricity]] element was destroyed in the [[700 IOG - Second Convergence|Second Convergence]]. This was not an accident or a tragedy in the way that the people who experienced it experienced it. It was a requirement of the next cycle. I am sorry for what it costs a world to lose a whole element. I am not sorry for the mechanism, which was necessary.

From eight to seven. Now, the seven have become the six. The six will, in the end, become something else. What it becomes depends on the Ascension. It has always depended on the Ascension.

I will not write more about this here. The Texts say what needs to be said about the Ascension. I have written in this journal long enough tonight.

――――――――――――

# vii. what I miss, because apparently I am writing that kind of memoir tonight

Sere’s voice. She had a way of speaking that made everything she said sound like it was being said for the last time, with full awareness that it was the last time, and full acceptance of this. I spent a long time thinking this was affectation. It was not.

The way the world felt when the gods were present in it. Not their instructions. Not their demands. Not the Court rituals and the endless protocol of divine attendance. The feeling. The way the air had weight. The way certainty of a particular kind — not faith, not belief, something more sensory than either — was simply available.

Atiri arguing with me. I know this is sentimental. I am old enough to be sentimental without apology.

The eastern forests before the trade routes turned them to resources. The great cats who would not speak to you unless they felt like it, which they rarely did, which made it better when they did.

Not being the last. That is the one I circle back to most often, late in the night. It is not grief exactly; I have had too long to process the grief and whatever is left of it has changed into something I do not have an accurate name for. But not being the last would have been — would still be — something.

I have been called the last so many times by so many different people that I have almost started to believe it myself. Almost.

――――――――――――

# viii. the present moment, which I am not going to explain

There are six of them now. More or less. One is already moving and does not yet know why. The stone found him in the mountains because the stone knows its own timing, not mine.

The Texts are where they need to be. The woman should have them now, and the Texts will do what the Texts do, and she, and hopefully the rest, will climb the mountain.

The mountain is patient. The mountain has waited this long.

I am aware that writing “I am not going to explain” in a heading and then continuing to write is precisely the kind of thing Atiri used to do, and precisely the kind of thing I used to criticise him for. I am leaving it anyway.

There is a boy in the city who is going to burn everything down, if he is not careful, and also if he is careful. Fire is like that. He does not yet know who he is and he does not yet need to. He has been surviving longer than he should have been able to and he does not know why. He will find out.

There is a woman walking away from an arrangement that was made without her knowledge for purposes she does not yet understand, carrying something in her hands that has been trying to reach her for more than a thousand years. The Texts found the right pair of hands. They always do, when I put them somewhere reasonable. I will take credit for that much.

There is a man who lifts impossible things and does not fully understand yet that lifting impossible things is the least of what he can do. The stone knew him. The stone knows.

There is a girl hiding who she is inside a borrowed title, and the earth knows her name even if the people around her do not.

There is a man made of grief who talks to the dead and is surprised when they answer. The dead have always answered people like him. He is simply the first in a long time who could hear it.

Ice seems to be gathering around a prince's stone cold heart and his catfire friend. She knows of this but he does not. It is the first time I have seen a shard choose two instead of one, maybe it is the remnant of electricity that causes the problem. It is a wonder why they haven't noticed they keep running into each-other.

And somewhere — I am choosing not to know where, for now — there is a wind that has not found its stone yet. That is the one I watch for. That is the one that determines whether this cycle resolves the way the previous ones did not.

I am going to the mountain soon. Not yet. There is one more thing to put in place first, and then I am going, and I will be there when they arrive, and I will be whatever I need to be when they arrive, and that is all I am going to say about it here.

This journal has been a document of what I remember. Let the record show: I remember almost everything. The things I have chosen to forget are chosen with purpose, and they remain in their place, and I do not regret the choice.

What I have poured into others has not diminished me in the way I once expected it to. Atiri was wrong about many things; he was right that knowledge is not power but perception. I gave him everything I knew and I still know it. It works like light, not like water. You do not have less of it because you have given some away.

That is a comfort. I note it here for the benefit of anyone who comes after and finds themselves in a similar position, which is unlikely, given that I am the last of a particular kind of person, but not impossible.

— V.

do not let them climb alone

that is the only rule that matters

========================================

---
title: Grave of Hasharshagetes
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

# Text on the Grave
**Hasharshagetes**
"He who saw the dawn of an ancient age is now a seed of the night."

# The Myth
In the grey-light of the First **Za**, when the names of the stars were yet unwritten and the gods had not yet carved their laws into the heavens, there walked **Haʃarʃagetes**. He was a man of the [[Bon]]. He was a soul who refused the power of a lord and the earthen promises of the house-master. While others sought the warmth of the fires of the hearth, he sought only the edge of the world.

"I shall be the breath of [[Aushuzi|the dawn]]," he declared to the silent stones. With a bronze blade, he shaped the boat, a vessel of fir to brave the wakes, and committed his fate to the seas. He sailed where the salt-spray stings with the fury of [[Shuzi|Dash]], crossing the vast, standing waters where the deep-gods dream. He was the first to track the tamagase - the spirit-signs - written in the foam and the flight of the white-birds.

Beyond the horizon’s veil, he reached the [[Mount Aemi|Zama]], the peak that hold the gates to the heavens above. He climbed until the air grew thin as a ghost’s whisper, higher than the bear dares to tread. All that accompanied him was the whispers of the zephyrs. There, in the silence of the high peaks, the veil was rent; waters succumbed to ice. He did not find jewels; he found **Ma**. He saw the Great Reality, the shimmering thread that binds the seed to the star, and the fires to the sun. In that moment of blinding light, he was no longer a traveler; he was the shadotor - the Seer who knows the weight of the world.

He left [[Elements|the seven]] where they should remain. On descent the man in white watched only observed in the corner of an eye.

But the night comes for every-one even those who walk the path of the shadotor. When his hands grew too weary to grasp the oar, he steered his boat home. He dropped his heavy anchor into the silt of the ancestral bay, not in surrender, but in completion. He laid his head upon the earth and became the very thing he had witnessed: a fragment of the cycle.

Now he rests beneath unmoving stone.

- **First Za** = first era, before the first convergence
- **Hakimu** = heavens
- **Zama** = mountain
- **Dash** = Sky god, king of the gods, Zeus, Jupiter, Dyeus Pater
- **Ma** = reality, truth

title: Riley

>[!infobox|wikipedia]
># Riley
>_Rogue_
>INSERT IMAGE HERE
>Born: [[Dating|16th of Minumi 1762 IOG]] (age 19), [[Amphos]], [[Eastern Solaran Empire]]
>Class: Rogue 3, Thief
>Background: Criminal
>Race: Half-Tabaxi, Tabaxi traits
>Languages: [[Common]] (Fluent when Spoken, Illiterate), [[Aeikas]] (modern) (mostly illiterate, Fluent when Spoken)
>Relatives: [[Zenshoran Hagashar]] (biological father), [[Tabtab]] (Half-sister), [[Campaign 2 - DM Notes/Notable NPCs/Wrensu]] (Adoptive father), Queen of the Eastern Solaran Empire (mother)
>Element: [[Fire]]

# Backstory
Riley was born of an affair between his father, [[Zenshoran Hagashar]], and his mother, the queen of Amphos. His father took him on the day of his birth out to the slums and abandoned him there as to not be discovered. He was laid in a barn next to some valuables. He was later found and adopted by [[Campaign 2 - DM Notes/Notable NPCs/Wrensu]], a goliath criminal who operates within [[Amphos]]. At the time he was linked with an underground revolutionary unit.

As he grew older he was told by Wrensu that he was born, in a barn, into a poor family and that his Tabaxi father was executed for his crimes by the royal family before I was born, and that his Human mother went into hiding. Wrensu told him that nobody was left to assist his mother during the birthing process.

When he turned four, Wrensu, a fellow rogue, began to show him how to pickpocket. He practiced the craft for years and by the time he was eight he could do execute the skill near-flawlessly. By the time he turned eleven he got his first knives. These helped him fight off competing thieves and attackers who targeted him and steal for no reason other than personal gain. Around the same age he got his first lute which he devoted himself to religiously.

Due to being half-tabaxi he has been cast aside for being too effeminate and if not he was taken advantage of. Tabaxi are also extremely rare and foreign to the people of Amphos, western [[As]] and [[Shul]], being native to the far-eastern kingdoms, especially [[Divine Empire of Daxing]] and countries further east of it. Because of the way people have treated him, he has trouble making true, genuine friends and trusting people.

He has had to embrace my feminine features and looks, and has learned to utilise them to take advantage of them. He has been able to convince others that he is, in-fact, a girl which has helped him acquire money and other resources in times of need. Feeding, at times, not only himself but others in the slums with him. Because of these actions he has started to be considered a local hero by the poor and those less fortunate. They have dubbed him "The Freedom Cat."

# Astragalomancy Prophecy
- **[[Hashos]]** - A spark dances at your fingertips. It will light your path and warm your hands, but do not grow complacent; even success can be fleeting when not honed.

title: Tabtab
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS

>[!infobox|wikipedia]
># Tabtab
>_Apothecary_
>INSERT IMAGE HERE
>Born: [[Dating|18th of Shumi 1764 IOG]] (age 17), [[Amphos]], [[Eastern Solaran Empire]]
>Race: Half-Tabaxi/Elf
>Relatives: [[Zenshoran Hagashar]] (biological father), [[Riley]] (Half-Brother), Unnamed Courtesan (Biological Mother)

# Backstory
**Tabtab** is a 17-year-old half-tabaxi/half-elf (catfire) whose life is defined by a deep expertise in medicinal arts and a penchant for solving complex puzzles, fitting the mould of an apothecary. Standing at a petite height and slender weight , she possesses dark hair and fair skin. She frequently uses makeup or clay to mask her features, opting to appear "plain" or sickly to avoid unwanted attention. Perhaps her most striking physical characteristic is the collection of scars lining her arms, remnants of her obsessive habit of testing various toxins and poisons on her own body.

## Early Life and Training
Born in the bustling Pleasure District of [[Amphos]] in the [[Eastern Solaran Empire]], Tabtab was raised by her foster father, a former court physician. Under his mentorship, she developed a scientific worldview, prioritising empirical evidence and cause-and-effect over faith in the divine or destiny. During this time she was working as an apprentice apothecary for the premier Brothel in the district. This also happens to be where her mother, who is a victim of  syphilis due to becoming less valued after having Tabtab, resides in secret, out of view. Her father [[Zenshoran Hagashar]] frequents here attempting to buy both Tabtab and her mother, but his patronage is rejected due to his inability to buy Tabtab's mother earlier and Tabtab's hatred of him.

The education she received from her father and the brothel provided her with the skills necessary to navigate both the herbalist's shop and the dangerous political landscapes she would later inhabit. Her quiet life of gathering herbs was interrupted when she was kidnapped by traffickers and sold into domestic service within the Imperial Court of Amphos.

## Initial Service in the Court
Throughout her initial appointment at the court she is discovered by [[Tukue Potes]], as someone who is more educated than the rest of the servants and had helped prevent a miscarriage and death of the consort to the emperor [[Bardashes]]. She was hired by one of the consort as one of her ladies-in-waiting, throughout this time she grew closer to Tukue Potes and has been noticed by him and her services requested when there was a problem he could not solve alone and required extensive intrigue and courtly gossip.

Eventually she was fired in a court-wide shakeup.

## Return to the Court
After her initial dismissal, Tabtab is brought back to the Court by Tukue Potes. Her primary mission in is to serve as the chief food taster and protector for a Consort, whose second pregnancy must be kept a strictly guarded secret to avoid the political backstabbing. During this time, Tabtab acts as the first line of defence against the constant threat of assassination and medical negligence targeting the imperial heir.

## Understanding Tukue Potes
The most significant shift in Tabtab's history occurs during a royal hunt. While attending to Tukue Potes, she discovers the secret he has been hiding behind the façade of a eunuch: he is an intact male. This discovery forces her to confront the reality of the prince's true identity as the heir (or potential protender) to the throne of Amphos. Despite her desire to remain an indifferent observer, she is now burdened with a secret that could lead to the execution of everyone involved.

# Personality and Disposition
Tabtab is a dedicated introvert who generally avoids social interaction unless it is necessary for her work or safety. In conversation, she is known for a direct, dry, and often blunt delivery. While she is content to act as a follower and maintain a façade of respect toward authority, she internally challenges any ideas she finds logically unsound. She is not motivated by money or status, but rather by the pursuit of knowledge and the safety afforded by her group. Her greatest vice is an insatiable curiosity regarding poisons, which often overrides her sense of self-preservation.

## Ambitions and Outlook
In the short term, Tabtab is driven by the acquisition of rare medicinal ingredients and alchemical knowledge. Her broader, long-term goals involve advancing the field of medicine and securing a future where she can pursue her research freely, far removed from the high-stakes tyranny of courtly life. Despite her cynical exterior, she possesses a Neutral Good alignment, often helping those in need - especially when a medical mystery is involved - even if she claims to do so only for the sake of the puzzle.

FILE: Campaign 2 - DM Notes\Notable NPCs\The Court of Amphos\Tukue Potes.md
========================================

---
title: Tukue Potes
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

>[!infobox|wikipedia]
># Tukue Potes
>_Prince of Amphos, Moon Prince_
>INSERT IMAGE HERE
>Born: [[Dating|15th of Narimi 1765 IOG]] (age 16), [[Amphos]], [[Eastern Solaran Empire]]
>Race: Human
>Relatives: [[Bardashes]] (Imperial Brother)

# Backstory
**Tukue Potes** is a high-ranking official and the primary administrator of the Lower Court, the secluded residence of the [[Bardashes|Emperor]]’s consorts. While he initially presents himself as a high-status eunuch, his true identity, as the Heir to the Throne of the [[Eastern Solaran Empire]], and physical status remain one of the most guarded secrets within the Imperial Court. Known for his "celestial beauty," Tukue Potes uses his appearance as both a shield and a weapon to maintain order in a den of political vipers.

## Administrator of the Lower Court
Tukue Potes functions as the "manager" of the Emperor's women. He discovers [[Tabtab]] after she solves the mystery of the dying imperial infants and quickly recognizes her unique value. Throughout this period, Tukue Potes is characterized by his "honeyed mask"—a façade of perfect, radiant charm that he uses to manipulate consorts and officials alike. However, he grows increasingly frustrated by Tabtab’s unique immunity to his charms, which eventually blossoms into a genuine, albeit awkward, romantic fixation. His primary role involves mitigating the "Honey Poison" incident and managing the fallout of the attempted assassination of Consort Rishi.

## Reveal and Ritual
During a strategic hunting trip, his true physical nature - that he is not a eunuch, but an "intact" man - is discovered by Tabtab. This revelation clarifies his true status as the Imperial Brother (and potential heir), a role he finds stifling.

His administrative brilliance during his trial of the Shrine of Choosing. Tukue Potes is tasked with navigating the ritualistic and architectural puzzles of the imperial ancestors. While he relies on Tabtab’s scientific deductions to solve the "miracle" of the coloured doors, it is his political manoeuvring that allows the Emperor to maintain face and authority during the visiting envoys' stay.

# Personality and Relationships
Tukue Potes is a man of contradictions: a powerful statesman who is secretly insecure, and a "celestial" figure who acts like a petulant child when his plans are foiled. His relationship with his aide, Gotinos, provides the emotional backbone of his life, as Gotinos is one of the few people who treats him as a human rather than an icon. Tukue Potes's interest in Tabtab has shifted from professional curiosity to a deep-seated need for her presence, even as he realises that bringing her closer to him puts her in the crosshairs of imperial politics.

FILE: Campaign 2 - DM Notes\Notable NPCs\The Court of Amphos\Zenshoran Hagashar.md
========================================

---
title: Zenshoran Hagashar
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

>[!infobox|wikipedia]
># Zenshoran Hagashar
>_Donpotes da Tagaminase_
>INSERT IMAGE HERE
>#### Donpotes da Tagaminase
>Predecessor: Danos
>Years of Service: 1760 IOG - Present
>###
>Born: 23 Hanoshi 1734 IOG, [[Divine Empire of Daxing]]
>Spouses: None
>Issue: [[Riley]], [[Tabtab]]
>Allegiance: [[Eastern Solaran Empire]]

# Biography

Born in the mist-shrouded peaks of the [[Divine Empire of Daxing|Eastern Realms]], **Zenshoran Hagashar** did not inherit his status; he carved it out of tactical necessity. After mastering the arts of war in his homeland, he travelled to the [[Eastern Solaran Empire|Solari heartland]] on a diplomatic mission, where his "demonstrated knowledge" of troop manoeuvres and logistics earned him the rare trust of the **[[Puli]]**.

However, his rise was nearly halted by a significant experience: a clandestine affair with the Puli's wife. The resulting birth of his son, **[[Riley]]**, created a trauma that shifted his very alignment. To survive, Zenshoran was forced to disown the boy at birth. This secret guilt and the subsequent loss of the child to the Goliath **[[Campaign 2 - DM Notes/Notable NPCs/Wrensu]]** have become the deep-seated regrets that define his abrasive, cold exterior.

Now, as the _Donpotes da Tagaminase_ (head of military in the Eastern Solaran Empire), he functions as the Empire’s silent fist. He watches his daughter, **[[Tabtab]]** - born to a courtesan at a brothel that he was unable to buy -  move through the palace as an apothecary to the prince, unable to claim her, yet desperate to protect her, while his disowned son is raised in the slums to destroy everything Zenshoran has built. He is a man caught between the "Dawn" of his title and the "Shadow" of his past.

# Appearance

He wears ornate [[Setting/Cultures/Solari|Solari]] lamellar armour over deep crimson silks from the Eastern Realms. He moves with a silent, predatory grace that contrasts sharply with his rigid, bureaucratic posture. His most distinguishing feature is a long, jagged scar running through his left ear—a souvenir from a Goliath’s blade.

# Personality

- He is a leader who tends to leave people be, speaking only when he requires something or when addressed.
- Conversationalists find him direct and suave, though he often comes across as though he has something to hide.
- uses High-Imperial etiquette as a shield to hide his true emotions.
- He works with others because "a lone claw is easily snapped; a phalanx is a mountain".
- "I help those who function within the Imperial design. Mercy is a luxury for those not burdened with the defence of a realm"

## Ideals

- The Empire is a great water-clock; if one gear hesitates, the Sun itself loses time.
- A blade does not feel pity; it only feels the edge. I am the blade of the Bardashpotes.
- The stain on the silk cannot be washed, but it can be hidden beneath a deeper dye.

## Bonds

- He is emotionally attached to his Eastern blade, _Dawn-Sliver_
- He will stop at nothing to protect [[Tabtab]]
- He has personally prevented [[Riley]] from being killed by the City Watch in Amphos

## Flaws

- His arrogance regarding his own intellect makes him emotionally abrasive. He is traumatized by the scandal of Riley's birth- a "shame" he carries like a physical weight.

FILE: Campaign 2 - DM Notes\Notable NPCs\The Court of Brackenfall\Sirric Ethelrik.md
========================================

---
title: Sirric Ethelrik

password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

>[!infobox|wikipedia]
># Sirric Ethelrik
>_Leader of the Patushepatir_
>INSERT IMAGE HERE
>Born: [[Dating|15th of Shumi 1757 IOG]] (age 24), [[Armth County]], [[Brackenfall]]
>Race: Half-elf, moon-elf

# Biography

Born 24 years ago in the mountainous county of [[Armth]], Sirric Ethelrik was heir to the count of Armth, Derred Ethelrik. He grew up in the keep of the capital of Armth, within the comfort of a noble family of modest wealth. His mother died by the hands of [[Eastern Solaran Empire|Amphosian]] raiders at age 10. A year later, seeing the weakness in the county, an occupation force from the [[Brackenfall|Duchy of Brackenfall]] entered the county, resulting in its annexation. The violent event created a land border between Brackenfall and the Amphosian Despotate. The Duchy of Brackenfall then razed his city, his home. It is yet to recover to its former state.

Feeling oppressed under unfamiliar and illegitimate rule, his father began fomenting a rebellion to restore the sovereignty of the county and his house.

At the age of 14, by the order of the Duke of Brackenfall, Sirric was forced to watch as his father and all adults found complicit, or otherwise aiding, the rebellion, were executed. In the same horrible moment, a dragon - whether mysteriously summoned, or drawn by the bloodshed remains unknown - attacked the capital of Brackenfall. After unleashing hell-fire upon the rebels and their families, it was killed upon a city spire. Sirric and the other children survived, though each bore burn scars along their arms.

Following this, Sirric was personally punished for being the son of the leader of the rebellion and was shunned throughout the dukedom. Everywhere he went, his name was spoken as a slur.

At the age of 16 he was conscripted to join the Brackenfallian elite forces, a collection of mage-knights designed to crush enemy incursions quickly and decisively. Despite his hatred for all things Brackenfallian, he was an exceptional soldier and earned several promotions with haste. Yet, he remains an outsider, obeyed for his rank, but never fully accepted, even by those he has aided. He was eventually granted his own battalion composed of his former kin, the children of the rebellion, officially called the "Patushepatir" (an [[Aeikas]] word borrowed from the Amphosian Despotate meaning a quarter quadrant), as they are the fourth battalion of the elite forces.

Now, at age 24 he has heard news that the [[Ellowen|heir to the Duchy of Brackenfall]] is to be betrothed to the [[Tukue Potes|Prince of the Amphosian Despotate]]. As he and his battalion march to [[Amphos]] for their diplomatic assignment to protect and escort the prince and his royal apothecary on his way to the holy city of [[Itrea]].

# Appearance

Sirric is a tall man (6' 0") with black hair and dark eyebrows. His facial features are marked by a strong jawline, and his skin is olive in colour. He often has dark stubble on his face and his body is muscular. There is a lethal grace to him. His eyes are distinctive, characterized by a shade of onyx speckled with flecks of gold. The dragon left a burn scar which starts at his left wrist and stretches all the way up his neck, stopping at his jawline. This has turned into black, almost like a tattoo. His voice has a rough pitch, but sounding like velvet. His lips are perfect. Sirric’s chest is massive, with wide shoulders and heavily muscled arms alongside. Every edge of his body is honed like a weapon. He smells of mint and leather and something that borders between citrus and floral.

# Personality

Sirric is a kind person at heart, but he has been forced to become a grim, success-oriented killer in a world that views him as a threat. All of his experiences have forced him to hide vulnerabilities and suppress emotions wherever he can. He keeps intense control over his feelings, rarely allowing others to see any sign of weakness or uncertainty. He approaches every interaction defensively, especially when he’s speaking with those in power or Brackenfallians. This emotional barrier tends to initially make Sirric appear detached and unapproachable. He is a secretive individual, closely guarding his own secrets, even from those he trusts. He places his trust in very few people and likes to keep it that way. He doesn’t hold as much faith in the rules, especially those set by the Brackenfall government, which is why he likes to command his own battalion his way. His disregard for these regulations is evident when he defies the law by meeting with more than three other children marked for rebellion outside of designated hours.

Condition Immunities [Blinded](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#BlindedCondition), [Charmed](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#CharmedCondition), [Deafened](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#DeafenedCondition), [Exhaustion](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#ExhaustionCondition), [Prone](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/free-rules/rules-glossary#ProneCondition)

Challenge 1/8 (25 XP)

![](https://www.dndbeyond.com/file-attachments/0/579/stat-block-header-bar.svg)

Traits
 **_Adorably Acidic._** A creature that touches Woubble or hits him with an attack while within 5 feet of him takes 1 acid damage.
 **_Gelatinous._** A creature within 5 feet of Woubble can take an action to pull an creature or object out of Woubble. Doing so requires a successful DC 8 Strength check, and the creature making the attempt takes 2 (1d4) acid damage.
 Woubble can hold up to one Tiny creature or four Tiny objects at a time. A creature or object inside Woubble can be seen but has total cover.
 **_Bouncy._** Woubble's long jump is up to 10 feet and his high jump is up to 10 feet, with or without a running start.
Actions
 **_Blorp Blorp._** _Melee Weapon Attack:_ +0 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. _Hit:_ 1 acid damage.
 **_Huggable Barrier._** Woubble activates a protective barrier around themself, which lasts for 1 minute or until Woubble dismisses it (no action required). While the barrier is active, Woubble’s AC is 10, other creatures automatically succeed on Dexterity saving throws against Engulf, and friendly creatures that touch Woubble take no damage from their Adorably Acidic trait.
 **_Engulf._** Woubble moves up to his speed. While doing so, he can enter the space of other creatures. Whenever he enters the space of a Tiny creature, the creature must make a DC 8 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2 (1d4) acid damage and is engulfed. The engulfed creature can’t breathe, is restrained, and takes 4 (2d4) acid damage at the start of each of Woubble’s turns. When Woubble moves, the engulfed creature moves with him. 
 An engulfed creature can try to escape by taking an action to make a DC 8 Strength check. On a success, the creature escapes and enters a space of its choice within 5 feet of Woubble.
Bonus Actions
 **_Encourage._** Woubble can take the Help action as a bonus action to assist a creature within 30 feet of him.

FILE: Campaign 2 - DM Notes\Notable NPCs\Party Companions\Ulriki.md
========================================

---
title: Ulriki
password: HIDE_FROM_PLAYERS
---

A young impoverished boy of [[Setting/Cultures/Solari|Solari]] descent from the town of [[Jentan|Jantani]] in the [[Caliphate of Lqlima]]. He wondered for 270 days from Jantani to [[Nymphi]], east across the desert, entering the [[Eastern Solaran Empire]] to [[Aktos|Aktosi]], travelling further east, crossing the wild plains of the [[Raurorumia Province]] to [[Athia|Athiai]], North East to join the Everlasting Trail to [[Leipathi]] and [[Pithumemi]] ([[Iponiaros Province]]), crossing into the [[Delphidria Province]], north west to [[Agrara]], then north to [[Nauros]] and [[Paphi]] in the same province. He then continued North to cross into the province of [[Rhithon Province|Rhithon]] arriving solely at the town of [[Akhalarynt]] before continuing to [[Thergan Province]] where he went to [[Nelionti]], when he finally ended up in the province of [[Athmolis Province|Athmolis]], first arriving at [[Hubros]] then continued to [[Byrian]], [[Byblostos]], [[Ampianagri]], [[Doryrena]], [[Pyrma]], [[Byblarascu]] then finally [[Akrossa]], where he spent 3 months trying to accrue food and money to continue travelling to [[Wiesen]] in [[Brackenfall]].
